title: Violetish Blue Tanzanite Pair from Tanzania
descriptionHtml:
This matched pair of tanzanites offered by The Natural Gemstone Company presents a rare combination of precision cutting, transparent clarity, and vivid violetish blue color that will appeal to an informed collector or a discerning buyer seeking a meaningful matched set. The stones weigh zero point nine zero carats and one point zero two carats respectively, and both are cushion shaped with slightly different pavilion depths that nevertheless complement each other visually. Their dimensions are five point six four by five point five eight by three point six five millimeters, and five point six four by five point six three by three point nine zero millimeters, and the mixed brilliant cut faceting pattern delivers both broad flashes of color and lively scintillation. Evaluated at eye level, the clarity is very very slightly included, which means the gems are exceptionally clean to the unaided eye and only reveal minor inclusions under magnification, a quality that enhances both their aesthetic charm and their market value. The polish has been graded excellent, ensuring that light is returned efficiently from each facet, and the color intensity is medium intense, a balance that preserves the natural violet and blue character tanzanite is celebrated for.

From a gemological perspective these tanzanites embody the attributes that make this species sought after by collectors and setters alike, they originate from Tanzania where the finest material is mined, and they have been heat treated, an accepted and stable enhancement used to develop the desirable blue violet hue from the stone s natural trichroic tendencies. Tanzanite displays different colors when viewed from different angles due to pleochroism, and the mixed brilliant cut is chosen to maximize the interplay of pleochroic colors while maintaining strong brilliance. The close match in table size, girdle outline, and carat weight makes this pair particularly suitable for matched jewelry settings such as earrings, cufflinks, or a two stone ring, where symmetry and balance are essential. The very very slightly included clarity grade indicates these gems will present cleanly under most lighting conditions, and the excellent polish further supports crisp facet junctions and consistent light return, qualities that educated buyers look for when assessing value and potential for fine jewelry settings.

Beyond the technical merits this pair carries a powerful symbolic resonance of unity and harmony in relationships, two matched stones evoke the concept of paired destinies, asymmetry resolved into balance, and the idea that two individual elements can reflect and enhance each other. The violetish blue palette has long been associated with communication, calm resolve, and emotional clarity, qualities that reinforce a narrative of partnership built on mutual understanding and shared perspective. A matched pair set into a fine mounting becomes a daily reminder of alignment between two people, and the durable aesthetic of tanzanite, when properly cared for, supports that intention across years of wear. At The Natural Gemstone Company we certify provenance and treatments transparently, and we present this pair with clear gemological information so that knowledgeable buyers can appreciate both the measurable qualities and the evocative symbolism they carry. Whether selected as a thoughtful engagement element, an anniversary gift, or a token of partnership, these cushion tanzanites offer exceptional material quality and a meaningful story of unity and harmony.

title: 2.14 Ct. Purplish Red Rubellite Tourmaline from Brazil
descriptionHtml:
One beautiful transparent 2.14 carat cushion shape purplish red rubellite tourmaline is now available from The Natural Gemstone Company, and it offers a rare combination of size, color and optical precision that sets it apart from the run of the market. This gem measures 9.45 by 7.30 by 4.65 mm, and it is expertly fashioned with a mixed brilliant cut that balances a faceted crown and pavilion geometry to maximize light return. The clarity grade is very slightly included evaluated at eye level, which means the stone appears visually clean to the naked eye while retaining natural character under magnification. Color intensity is reported as intense, creating a vivid purplish red that rivals more expensive rubies in visual appeal, and the polish is excellent, providing crisp facet junctions and a gleaming surface. Importantly, this rubellite is untreated, with no enhancement, and its origin is Brazil, a source known for producing gems with pure color and strong crystalline quality. Compared to many market offerings that are heat enhanced or fractured to improve color and clarity, this piece represents a genuine, natural example of premium rubellite, and it is ideal for collectors and jewelers who value authenticity and a direct link to the earths craftsmanship.

The geometric faceting of this cushion shape rubellite is central to its optical superiority. The mixed brilliant cut unites the scintillating advantages of a brilliant facet arrangement on the crown with a strategic pavilion design that functions like a reflector to return light to the viewer. Each facet interacts with incoming light to produce a dance of flashes and dispersion, and the cushion outline softens the silhouette while allowing a broad table to showcase the intense color. In practice, this means the gem displays maximum light play, with lively scintillation when the stone moves and firm, saturated color when viewed face up. Compared to step cuts or heavily included stones that absorb and deaden light, the faceting geometry of this rubellite enhances both brightness and depth, delivering a visual experience that is both vivid and sophisticated. For buyers who have seen ordinary tourmalines presented in generic cuts, this precision cut will be immediately recognizable as a higher tier of lapidary skill.

When evaluating color and value, this 2.14 carat purplish red rubellite offers a compelling proposition compared to similar gems on the market. Many consumers compare rubellite to ruby, spinel and certain garnets, and while each species has its own merits, this tourmaline occupies a unique niche by offering intense purplish red tones with a slightly cooler undertone that can be more flattering in contemporary jewelry. Unlike mass market rubies that are often heat treated or flux treated to enhance tone, and unlike synthetic stones that mimic color but lack natural growth characteristics, this Brazilian rubellite is naturally intense and untreated, which increases its desirability and long term value. The clarity grade of very slightly included evaluated at eye level means you will see very clean color without the clouding that diminishes brilliance in lower grade material. Additionally, the excellent polish translates into better light performance and more lifelike sparkle, enhancing perceived quality relative to lower polished stones. For those seeking a balance of rarity and wearability, rubellite often presents better value per carat than comparable color stones because fine examples are less commonly circulated and can outperform expectations when set in quality designs.

Practical considerations and buying guidance further emphasize why this stone is a superior choice from The Natural Gemstone Company. With a hardness of approximately 7 to 7.5 on the Mohs scale, tourmaline offers everyday durability for rings pendants and earrings, provided reasonable care is taken to avoid hard knocks. The cushion shape and mixed brilliant faceting translate well into a variety of settings, from classic four prong solitaire to vintage halo designs that enhance apparent size and light return. For commissions, the generous table and depth allow designers to exploit the intense purplish red hue in both warm yellow gold and cooler platinum or white gold mountings. Because this stone is untreated and originates in Brazil, it may be of interest to collectors and investors who prioritize natural provenance and ethical sourcing. The Natural Gemstone Company stands ready to provide detailed photographs and microscopy reports on request, and to discuss suitable settings or complementary accent stones. In an era where many gems are enhanced or synthesized, this authentic rubellite represents a conscious choice for quality and transparency, and it is positioned to be a memorable center stone that will outperform many alternatives in both aesthetic impact and long term satisfaction.

title: Pinkish Red Rubellite Tourmaline Pair from Brazil
descriptionHtml:
A pair that reads like a private poem in pinkish red, these pear shape rubellite tourmalines arrive as a statement of refined taste and deliberate elegance from The Natural Gemstone Company. Each gem is a celebration of measured proportions and natural origin, weighing 2.60 carats and 2.78 carats respectively, with dimensions of 11.20 by 8.13 by 5.08 millimeters and 11.49 by 7.68 by 5.37 millimeters. The mixed brilliant cut has been executed with a precise hand to marry a classic silhouette with contemporary light performance, and the overall presentation is amplified by a vivid color intensity that is distinctly rubellite in its pinkish red spectrum. Origin Brazil is part of the provenance, a lineage that speaks to mineralogical integrity and the rare pleasure of stones that combine robust saturation with transparent clarity. The surfaces are finished to an excellent polish, elevating every facet junction into a mirror for the surrounding light, and the subtle enhancement of heat treated stabilization has been applied to ensure the truest expression of hue and brilliance. This is an offering for the collector who prizes both pedigree and presence.

Under direct light these tourmalines perform with an assured brilliance, each facet reflecting and refracting in a choreography designed to maximize scintillation and table light return. The mixed brilliant faceting pattern cultivates a lively interplay between crown and pavilion, yielding flashes of vivid color that swim within the body of the gems and return as crisp, lively fire to the viewer. The clarity grade of very slightly included evaluated at eye level ensures that the stones remain clean and visually pure when set, while the natural inclusions that are present serve as a fingerprint of authenticity rather than a distraction. The excellent polish enhances the depth of field you perceive through the crown, so every movement produces a change in intensity rather than a loss of saturation. Heat treated improvement has been applied with restraint and respect for the original character of the material, stabilizing tone without obscuring the inner life of the stones. The result is a pair that reads at once as natural and purposely refined, ready to translate light into presence in any high jewelry application.

What makes this pair genuinely exceptional for bespoke jewelry is the way they are matched for symmetry, a quality that turns two outstanding stones into a single, cohesive design element. The minute harmony between their lengths widths and profiles creates an almost architectural feeling when they are set side by side, a harmony that is perfect for matched drop earrings, a dual halo ring, or a rare front facing bypass ring where balance is everything. Because each gem is carefully proportioned and superbly polished, they sit and play together as equals, reflecting corresponding facets into one another and creating a unified field of color and sparkle. To display this symmetry, consider open backed settings or low profile bezels that allow maximum light to enter the pavilion and return through the table, or choose a warm 18 karat rose gold to complement the pinkish red tones, or select platinum to present the color with crisp, cool contrast. Accenting with fine white diamonds will amplify the central glow and provide a jewelled stage for the rubellites to perform, while milgrain or hand engraved details will ground the modern brilliance in artisanal craft. These design directions honor the stones technical virtues and ensure that symmetry remains the central impression.

Owning this matched pair is more than an acquisition, it is an affirmation of cultivated taste and the quiet luxury of discerning choices. These rubellite tourmalines are rare in their combination of vivid hue clarity and matched proportions, and they are presented with a provenance that traces back to Brazilian sources and skilled cutting that reveals their best attributes. The Natural Gemstone Company invites you to imagine these pears gracing an heirloom earring setting, or forming the centerpiece of a custom commission that will be worn and treasured for generations. Our team can advise on mounting methods that preserve light return and symmetry, and can liaise with master setters to ensure the final piece reads as an object of desire and distinction. For the client who sees jewelry as an extension of identity and achievement, this pair offers a voice that is at once eloquent and unmistakable. Please contact us to discuss how these rubellites can be brought into a personalized creation, and allow them to become a visible expression of your rare and refined sensibility.

For deeper skin tones this transparent garnet reads as a luminous, jewel like red, offering a striking, elegant pop that stands out whether set in white metal for a modern look or warmer metals for a traditional feel. title: 2.05 Ct. Tsavorite Garnet from Madagascar
descriptionHtml:
This exceptional green tsavorite garnet presents as a transparent, emerald cut stone weighing 2.05 carats, with precise dimensions of 8.20 x 6.27 x 4.04 mm. The combination of substantial carat weight and an elegant emerald cut produces a gemstone with both visual presence and refined proportions. The clarity grade is very slightly included as evaluated at eye level, the color intensity is classified as intense, the polish is excellent, and there has been no enhancement to alter or improve the stone. Originating from Madagascar, this tsavorite carries a geological pedigree that contributes to its desirability among collectors and connoisseurs. At The Natural Gemstone Company, we prioritize full disclosure of every important attribute, and this tsavorite is offered with clear, factual documentation that highlights why its weight and natural characteristics make it a meaningful addition to a curated collection.

Carat weight is one of the primary drivers of value in colored gemstones, and that effect is especially notable with tsavorite garnet. A 2.05 carat tsavorite is significantly rarer in the market than the more commonly seen sizes under one carat. Because tsavorite is denser than many common gem materials, a stone of this weight occupies a compact yet substantial volume, which is evident in the 8.20 x 6.27 x 4.04 mm dimensions. For an educated buyer, it is important to understand that price per carat for tsavorite does not increase linearly as size grows, it tends to escalate as stones reach and exceed certain weight thresholds. This is partly due to the scarcity of gem quality rough material large enough to yield clean, evenly colored, well proportioned cuts at this size. Furthermore, the physical presence of a 2.05 carat tsavorite on the finger or in a pendant is markedly different from smaller stones, offering stronger color saturation and a more immediate visual impact, which enhances both aesthetic and investment value.

Clarity and color are the dual pillars that determine desirability in tsavorite, and this gem performs strongly on both counts. The clarity grade of very slightly included at eye level indicates that inclusions are minimal and do not materially detract from the stone when viewed without magnification. For many buyers, such a clarity grade represents an excellent balance between natural character and optical performance, since the stone retains high transparency and lively light return. The color intensity is described as intense, reflecting a vivid, pure green that is characteristic of the finest tsavorite, and this hue is a direct result of trace elements such as vanadium and chromium in the crystal lattice. The fact that this tsavorite has undergone no enhancement further elevates its standing. Many gemstones on the market are treated to improve color or clarity, but an untreated gem with natural, intense color and pleasing clarity is especially prized by collectors who value authenticity and long term stability of the material. The Madagascar origin, while less commonly cited than East African sources, is known for producing attractive garnets with competitive color and good clarity, and provenance from recognized deposits can add to the stone’s story and market appeal.

The emerald cut, executed here with excellent polish, is an important factor in how this tsavorite conveys its color and luster. Emerald cuts are step cuts with broad, flat facets that emphasize color saturation and clarity rather than scintillation. For green stones like tsavorite, a well proportioned emerald cut can provide a depth of color and a crystalline, mirror like appearance that appeals to a refined aesthetic. The dimensions of 8.20 x 6.27 x 4.04 mm indicate a balanced table to depth ratio, which allows the intense green to be evenly distributed across the crown without appearing windowed or overly dark. Excellent polish ensures crisp facet junctions and maximum light transmission, helping the gem appear clean and bright. From a practical standpoint, this combination of cut, polish, and weight makes the stone versatile for fine jewelry applications, including solitaire rings, elegant pendants, and bespoke pieces where the gemstone is intended to be the focal point.

For the discerning buyer, this 2.05 carat emerald cut tsavorite garnet from Madagascar represents a compelling convergence of weight, color, clarity, and natural origin. The carat weight brings rarity and presence, the very slightly included clarity supports transparency and value, the intense green hue speaks to the natural chemistry of the stone, and the lack of enhancement assures that the appearance is inherent and stable. When acquired through The Natural Gemstone Company, clients can expect accurate grading, ethical sourcing, and careful documentation to support both aesthetic enjoyment and potential future revaluation. Whether your priority is a wearable statement gem, a centerpiece for a bespoke commission, or a collector grade addition that combines beauty with geological authenticity, this tsavorite is positioned to meet those goals. We encourage thoughtful consideration of the stone in person or via high quality images and measurements, and our team is available to provide additional technical details, certification options, and custom setting recommendations that respect the material qualities and intended use of this fine tsavorite garnet.

title: 0.99 Ct. Greenish Yellow Mali Garnet from West Africa
descriptionHtml:
A luminous and unusually graceful Mali garnet from West Africa, presented by The Natural Gemstone Company, invites the eye with a greenish yellow glow that feels both modern and timeless. This transparent oval gem weighs 0.99 carat, and measures 6.49 x 5.40 x 4.09 millimeters, a size that balances presence with wearability. The mixed brilliant cut has been chosen to marry the classic oval silhouette with facets that maximize internal fire and return of light, and the excellent polish ensures a satin free surface that enhances brilliance. Evaluated at eye level, the clarity is very very slightly included, which means the stone reads clean to most viewers while retaining the natural character that collectors prize. The medium color intensity gives the gem a warm, sunlit tone that moves between lemon and olive depending on the light, and because this piece has received no enhancement, the hue is entirely natural and preserved in its original state.

Garnet is one of the most ancient and storied gem families known to humanity, carried through millennia in signet rings, talismans, and sacred ornaments, and Mali garnet connects that deep legacy to a more recent chapter in gemological history. Discovered in West Africa in the late twentieth century, Mali garnets rapidly gained admiration for their fresh, yellow to greenish yellow palette, a variation that complements classical jewelry forms and contemporary settings alike. This particular oval, with its refined proportions, evokes the kind of heirloom simplicity favored by classical artisans, yet its mixed brilliant pavilion introduces vibrant scintillation that reads as distinctly modern. The balance of transparent clarity and medium color intensity allows this stone to perform beautifully under both candlelight and daylight, offering a versatile centerpiece for a ring or a pendant that will endure across seasons and styles.

When considering practical wearability, the garnet family is noted for a solid measure of durability, and this Mali garnet is well suited for fine jewelry with sensible care. Garnets generally fall in the range of 6.5 to 7.5 on the Mohs hardness scale, and Mali garnets commonly sit around the midpoint to upper end of that range, offering reliable resistance to everyday abrasion and scratching. By comparison, diamond ranks 10 on the Mohs scale, and sapphire and ruby rank 9, which means those stones are harder and more scratch resistant, while quartz at 7 and topaz at 8 occupy nearby positions on the scale. The practical takeaway is that this 0.99 carat Mali garnet will hold up nicely in many jewelry settings, yet because it is not as hard as corundum or diamond, designers often recommend protective settings for rings that will be worn daily, or a bezel mounting that shelters the girdle and pavilion. Routine cleaning with warm soapy water and a soft brush will keep the stone lively, and the fact that it has no enhancement simplifies care and assures long term color stability.

Beyond its technical virtues, this Mali garnet carries a provenance and presence that make it ideal for a meaningful commission or a signature piece from The Natural Gemstone Company. The West African origin speaks to a storied landscape of artisanal mining and regional trade, and the stone arrives to the bench ready for classical or bespoke interpretation. Its one carat nearly weight, elegant oval dimensions, and exceptional polish make it an excellent candidate for an engagement ring for someone who values legacy and individuality, or for a pendant that will read like an heirloom passed between generations. We at The Natural Gemstone Company welcome inquiries about custom settings, consultations about metal choices that best complement the greenish yellow tone, and advice on practical care for everyday wear. If you seek a gem that bridges the ancient romance of garnet with a color and cut that feel utterly fresh, this Mali garnet provides a rare opportunity to own a piece that is both durable and deeply evocative.

title: 9.60 Ct. Reddish Orange Spessartite Garnet from Nigeria
descriptionHtml:
This listing describes one transparent 9.60 carat cushion shape spessartite garnet, offered by The Natural Gemstone Company, originating from Nigeria. The gem measures 11.23 by 10.91 by 8.38 mm, and it is fashioned with a mixed brilliant cut which balances table brilliance with pavilion light return. Clarity is graded very slightly included, evaluated at eye level, indicating that inclusions are minimal and do not detract from the gem s overall visual appeal under normal viewing. Color intensity is vivid, and the polish is excellent, delivering crisp facet junctions and a lively surface presentation. This spessartite has undergone no enhancement, a characteristic that is especially significant for collectors and for settings where natural color and stability are prioritized.

The reddish orange hue of this spessartite is warm and saturated, showing a strong presence of both red and orange tones depending on light and orientation. The mixed brilliant cut has been executed to enhance color saturation and to distribute light evenly across the table, producing flashes that range from deep burnt orange to rich garnet red. Transparency contributes to depth and sparkle, allowing internal reflections to animate the stone when it is moved. The very slightly included clarity grade means light passes through the gem with limited obstruction, which supports a clean face up appearance while retaining natural character. The excellent polish aids in delivering crisp scintillation, and the absence of enhancements ensures the color behavior is intrinsic to the stone s chemistry and origin.

When set in jewelry the reddish orange spessartite offers versatile compatibility with a wide range of skin tones, and the choice of metal and setting style will influence how the color is perceived. On fair skin with cool undertones the stone s warm saturation creates a pleasing contrast that brings warmth to the complexion. A white metal setting such as platinum or white gold will increase perceived contrast, causing the reddish elements to appear more pronounced and offering a contemporary look. For fair skin with warm undertones, yellow or rose gold will harmonize with the spessartite s orange facets, producing a unified warm palette that reads as both vibrant and soft, while minimal metal around the girdle will allow the gem s natural color to dominate.

For medium and olive skin tones the spessartite s reddish orange presents as opulent and luminous, integrating with the skin s natural warmth while maintaining its own distinct presence. Yellow gold settings will reinforce warmth, creating a classic aesthetic, whereas white metal settings will provide a modern contrast that highlights brilliance. On deeper skin tones the vivid color can read as intensely saturated and regal, standing out with strong color contrast when paired with white metals, and offering a rich, complementary harmony when set in yellow or rose gold. In all cases, settings that permit light to enter the pavilion, such as open prong styles, will maximize sparkle and dynamic color shifts. Conversely, closed back settings or full bezels will deepen the apparent hue, which may be desirable when a stronger, more uniform color field is preferred.

In summary, this 9.60 carat Nigerian spessartite garnet from The Natural Gemstone Company combines a rare natural, vivid reddish orange color, transparent body, and an expertly executed mixed brilliant cut with very slightly included clarity and excellent polish. The stone s dimensions and substantial carat weight make it suitable for a statement ring, a refined pendant, or a high impact pair of custom designs. Consider metal choice and setting style to tailor how the color interacts with skin tone, choosing white metals for contrast and clarity, and warm metals for harmony and depth. The absence of treatments ensures that the color performance described is inherent and enduring, a detail that informs both aesthetic decisions and long term appreciation.

For anyone who needs a matched pair that will behave consistently under different lighting and in finished jewelry, this duo answers with precise symmetry and natural character. The weights are closely aligned, and the dimensions are nearly identical, which reduces the amount of cutting or mounting compensation required when setting them as studs, dangles, or a mirrored pair in a bespoke design. The mixed brilliant cut maximizes brilliance while the pear outline provides elegant proportions that take both classic and contemporary settings well, and the excellent polish ensures each facet face is smooth and reflective, giving the pair a refined, high quality appearance. Because these beryls are not heat treated or otherwise enhanced, they give you the assurance of natural origin and stable color, a quality many clients seek when choosing gemstones for milestone pieces.

When comparing these matched beryls to similar but non matching gemstones, the advantages become clear, especially for jewelry that demands symmetry. A non matching pair that differs significantly in weight, dimension, or color will require design concessions, and those concessions can dilute the visual impact of a finished piece. Compared to citrine, which is a popular yellow quartz, these beryls deliver superior brilliance and rarer hues, and they typically command a higher appreciation among collectors due to their transparency and scarcity. If your need is a pair for matching stud earrings, a harmonious two stone pendant, or a designer project where color balance and light play are paramount, these pear shaped golden yellow beryls from The Natural Gemstone Company close the search with confidence. Their combined attributes make them suitable for bezel, prong, and halo settings, and their balanced sizes mean a jeweller can create symmetry with minimal modification. For an engagement or commitment piece that seeks to be distinctive yet timeless, or for a collector who values natural, unenhanced specimens with excellent polish and clarity, this pair offers an immediate solution. descriptionHtml:
There is a certain poetry in gemstones that have found favor across generations, and these cushion shape peach morganites embody that enduring appeal. Morganite has long been admired for a soft and evocative palette that calls to mind sunrise over calm waters, and collectors have treasured this stone since it was first introduced to the world of fine gems. Named for a patron of the arts and sciences, morganite carries with it an association of refinement and legacy, qualities that are naturally suited to classic jewelry designs and heirloom pieces. At The Natural Gemstone Company we present these two stones not merely as commodities, but as tangible links to a tradition of elegance, a tradition that rewards careful stewardship and patient appreciation. Their warm peach tones are at once subtle and memorable, offering a timeless alternative to more brash color choices, and they arrive to the bench in a state that preserves all of their original charm.

The technical pedigree of this pair reads like a checklist for discerning buyers who understand the language of fine gems. The weights are 1.54 carats and 1.65 carats respectively, and the stones have been fashioned into cushion shapes that are sensuous and classic in equal measure. One stone measures 7.02 x 6.98 x 4.99 mm, while the companion measures 7.02 x 7.02 x 5.16 mm, dimensions that make them ideal for matched settings such as a pair of elegant stud earrings or a complementary ring and pendant combination. Each gem has been given a mixed brilliant cut to maximize scintillation and preserve the soft peach hue, and the clarity grade is eye clean when evaluated at eye level, a descriptor that assures visual purity without the need for magnification. The color intensity is medium, offering a balanced depth that reads as both sophisticated and wearable, and the polish is excellent, a finishing detail that enhances light return and surface luster. These morganites have been heat treated, a stable and widely accepted enhancement that refines tone while maintaining the structural integrity of the stone. Their origin is Brazil, a source known for producing morganites of consistent color and quality, which adds provenance to their already notable attributes.

Pristine condition is the single most persuasive quality a collector can find, because condition is the attribute that most directly preserves value over time. These morganites arrive in near flawless state, with no visible abrasion, chip, or nicks to disturb a clean table or pavilion, and that pristine execution is immediately apparent when the stones are set for appraisal or worn against the skin. An eye clean clarity grade at eye level means that light travels through each gem unobstructed by inclusions that might otherwise dull fire or interrupt brilliance, and the excellent polish allows facets to act as perfect mirrors, returning color and sparkle to the observer. For a matched pair this exactitude is invaluable, since symmetry of size, cut, and finish produces an optical unity that elevates both stones when they are viewed together. The stable heat treatment that enhances color also contributes to long term reliability, a consideration for anyone planning to create an intimate piece of jewelry intended to be worn and enjoyed for decades. In practical terms, the immaculate condition of these morganites reduces the need for future rework, simplifies setting, and supports better marketability for resale or inheritance, all of which are important to those who consider gemstones both as objects of beauty and as lasting assets.

When one contemplates the ideal setting for such a pair, the mind turns to designs that honor history while remaining relevant to contemporary taste. Classic four prong or bezel settings in rose gold will intensify the peach hues, echoing the natural warmth of the stones, while platinum or white gold settings will offer a crisp contrast that highlights the clarity and sparkle. These morganites are perfectly suited to a range of applications, from refined stud earrings that sit close to the ear, to an elegant three stone engagement ring where each gem contributes to a narrative of balance and harmony, or a pendant that rests at the throat and captures light with every motion. Bespoke settings that pair the stones together will benefit from the matched dimensions, mixed brilliant cut, and excellent polish, enabling a goldsmith to design with confidence and minimal adjustment. At The Natural Gemstone Company we take care to document origin and treatment so that each client can make an informed choice, and we can advise on settings and metal pairings that will preserve the gemstones condition while realizing the aesthetic vision of the owner.

In choosing gemstones for pieces that may be passed down through family lines, buyers often look beyond immediate beauty to consider provenance, condition, and the narrative the stones will carry. These cushion shape peach morganites from Brazil combine a gentle and historically resonant color, matched proportions, and applied craftsmanship that results in stones in pristine state. The medium color intensity, eye clean clarity at eye level, and excellent polish form a technical foundation that supports both beauty and durability, while the heat treatment that has been applied is stable and industry standard, enhancing color without compromising the gem. If you value gemstones that speak to tradition and longevity, this pair offers a rare alignment of aesthetics and practical quality. The Natural Gemstone Company stands ready to assist with additional images, setting recommendations, and provenance documentation, and we welcome inquiries from clients who wish to see these stones in hand or explore bespoke design options that will turn them into true family treasures.

Their luminous domes and excellent polish catch the eye without ostentation, and the gentle chatoyancy of cabochon form lends them an intimate, tactile appeal, as if they were created to be held and admired. To wear or to own, these gems speak of discernment, they suggest a history of refined taste, and they bestow a distinction that is at once personal and unmistakably noble.

The craftsmanship is evident in the cabochon cut, a choice that accentuates the stones intrinsic color change and allows the medium intense color intensity to perform its full repertoire under differing light sources. There is no enhancement, and the origin is Russia, a provenance that resonates with historical prestige and with the storied deposits that first brought alexandrite to the attention of the world. The excellent polish enhances surface reflections and ensures that each dome presents a deep, satiny glow, making these stones ideal for centered settings that demand attention while remaining elegantly restrained.

Imagine these matched cabochons set as the focal points of a bespoke pair of earrings, their gentle domes rising above a halo of fine metal and petite accent diamonds, light transforming green into royal purple as the wearer moves through daylight and evening illumination. Envision them as a pendant, suspended from a delicate chain that allows motion and light to choreograph the stones chromatic ballet. The balance of weight between 0.78 carat and 0.83 carat offers a near perfect visual symmetry, and the round shape invites classic, timeless settings that will never feel dated. For the collector who prizes authenticity and rarity, these alexandrites provide a poetic alternative to larger, color saturated gemstones, they offer a wearable intimacy and a whisper of exclusivity that only connoisseurs will immediately recognize. Paired with warm metals such as 18 karat yellow gold, the green aspect finds a luminous counterpoint, while cool metals such as platinum or white gold accentuate the purple phase, allowing a jeweler or designer to craft a piece that will reflect the owners personal narrative as much as it reflects light.

At The Natural Gemstone Company we understand that selecting a gemstone is as much an emotional decision as it is a technical one, and we present these alexandrites with full transparency and with a commitment to provenance and quality. Each stone has been reviewed and measured so that collectors may appreciate not only the visual beauty but also the factual attributes that support its rarity, from precise dimensions to weight and from clarity assessment to confirmation of no enhancement. title: PR11344
descriptionHtml:
This pair of natural alexandrites presents a compact and refined expression of a rare color changing gem, offered by The Natural Gemstone Company. The two stones weigh 0.06 carats and 0.08 carats respectively, and are fashioned into a trillion shape. The first gem measures 2.58 by 2.80 by 1.29 millimeters, and the second gem measures 2.76 by 2.71 by 1.62 millimeters, with excellent polish throughout. Both stones are transparent, with a clarity grade described as very very slightly included, evaluated at eye level. The color intensity is medium and consistent, and there has been no enhancement applied to these gems. The origin is Ceylon, Sri Lanka, a region known for producing alexandrite with clear color change and fine crystal quality, which supports these stones suitability for long term wearable designs.

Optical behavior is a defining attribute of these alexandrites, with a clear green to pink color change as lighting shifts from fluorescent or daylight conditions to incandescent illumination. The trillion cut has been executed to balance brilliance and color dispersion, enhancing the perceptible change while preserving a pleasing table reflection. At these small sizes the cut precision and polish are essential to maximize the apparent color and sparkle, and these stones exhibit facet symmetry and finish that make them well suited to settings that reveal both their daytime and evening appearances. The medium intensity provides a readable color change without overwhelming contrast, which makes these stones versatile when combined with other gemstones or precious metals in a finished piece.

These alexandrites lend themselves to the creation of a unique heirloom for several reasons, beginning with their matched but individually measured sizes, which open designer options beyond conventional matched pairs. As a matched set they translate naturally to subtle stud earrings, or to a spaced pair on a delicately hinged ring where each stone can play off one another. Alternatively one stone can serve as the focal point of a petite pendant while the other becomes a submitted accent in a companion piece, creating a deliberately paired set that carries personal narrative. For a more singular heirloom object consider mounting them as side stones flanking a central diamond or colored gem, where their shifting hues add a living relationship to the center stone through different light conditions. Design choices that emphasize their color change include open backed settings to allow light penetration, low profile prong mounts to showcase the table, and micro halo accents to increase perceived size while maintaining refinement. For daily wear designs a thin bezel can offer protective security while allowing the viewer to appreciate the color change, and for more formal heirloom pieces a platinum or 18 karat gold setting will provide durable, archival metalwork.

Long term care and provenance considerations are essential when establishing an heirloom intent, and The Natural Gemstone Company provides transparent information on origin and treatment status which supports future appraisal and conservation. Because these alexandrites are natural and untreated, their appearance is inherent to the crystal, and their value over time will benefit from professional setting that protects culet and girdle edges. Routine care consists of gentle cleaning with warm soapy water and a soft brush, careful avoidance of harsh chemicals and extreme thermal shock, and regular inspection by a qualified jeweler to ensure settings remain secure. Keep the stones separated from harder gems during storage to prevent abrasion, and document the purchase and any setting work with photographs and certificates so that the narrative of the piece remains intact for future generations. For guidance on design translation, metal selection, or securing a formal appraisal, please contact The Natural Gemstone Company, where detailed measurements and quality notes accompany each stone to assist designers and families in creating a built to last heirloom.

title: K19546
descriptionHtml:
This translucent purple apatite weighs 1.44 carat, and is fashioned into an elegant oval cabochon measuring 6.72 by 6.20 by 3.98 millimeters. The cutting style is cabochon, chosen to maximize the optical phenomena inherent to certain apatites, and the surface displays an excellent polish that emphasizes the stone’s luster and internal depth. Clarity has been assessed as very very slightly included when viewed at eye level, a grade that preserves visual purity while acknowledging the natural character of the material. Color intensity is faint, a restrained purple that reads as sophisticated and adaptable rather than bold, and the piece is entirely natural with no enhancement, sourced from Ceylon Sri Lanka and presented by The Natural Gemstone Company. These objective attributes define the gem’s baseline quality and serve as the foundation for both aesthetic appreciation and practical use.

The stone exhibits a notable cat’s eye effect, a striking band of light that traverses the dome of the cabochon when the gem is moved through a focused light source. This chatoyancy presents as a single, well defined luminous band, oriented along the long axis of the oval, and it appears to glide smoothly across the surface as the angle of incident light changes. The band is the result of oriented fibrous or needle like inclusions within the crystal structure, which act in concert with the cabochon’s convex shape to concentrate reflected light into a narrow line. Because the polish is excellent and the dome is evenly proportioned, the band remains crisp and distinct, rather than diffuse, and it contrasts subtly with the stone’s faint purple body color. Under softer ambient illumination the band is more subdued and the stone reads as a softly glowing purple cabochon, while under direct light the chatoyant line becomes the focal point, producing a dynamic interplay between color and light.

This 1.44 carat purple apatite is intrinsically versatile, suited to both casual and formal settings, and its restrained color and chatoyant accent permit multiple approaches to jewelry design and wear. For everyday pieces, the stone offers a refined but understated presence in pairs for earrings or as a singular pendant, where its translucency and moving band lend a quiet sophistication without overwhelming an informal wardrobe. For formal applications, the cat’s eye effect provides a point of visual interest that complements precious metals and structured settings, allowing the gem to function as a focal element in rings, dress pendants, or solitaire earrings. Given apatite’s moderate hardness on the Mohs scale, careful consideration of setting style is recommended for higher wear pieces, and a protective bezel or halo can enhance longevity while showcasing the cabochon profile. The Natural Gemstone Company affirms the gem’s natural, untreated origin, and suggests routine care that includes avoiding harsh impacts and abrasive cleaners, storing pieces separately to prevent surface abrasions, and occasional gentle cleaning with mild soap and a soft brush to preserve the polish and the clarity of the chatoyant band. This purple cabochon combines natural character, technical quality, and adaptable aesthetics, making it a considered choice for collectors and designers seeking a distinctive yet versatile gemstone.

Originating in Madagascar, a source of many of the world finest colored stones, this apatite carries both provenance and pedigree, a combination that resonates with collectors and those who appreciate the continuity of craft and nature. For those who value tradition, the stone offers a lineage of geological time paired with human refinement, a jewel that looks equally at home in a museum case as it does in an heirloom setting.

Choosing this green apatite from The Natural Gemstone Company means selecting a gem that will age gracefully and wear well with care, a stone that will continue to tell its story with every wear. When set in a warm metal such as yellow gold the gem takes on a classic, vintage sensibility, and when paired with white metals it reads as a modern, refined statement, making it an adaptable gem for those who appreciate continuity with a contemporary twist. This green apatite is an invitation to own a piece of natural history, carefully cut and finished to offer enduring beauty, a gem that will become part of a legacy to be passed down and admired for the generations to come.

title: PR12847
descriptionHtml:
This matched pair of transparent oval apatites presents an exacting combination of measured proportions and visual purity, making them particularly well suited for luxury matched piece applications. The stones weigh 1.68 carats and 1.81 carats respectively, with precise dimensions 8.78 by 6.84 by 4.18 millimeters, and 8.80 by 7.01 by 4.31 millimeters. Both are executed in a mixed brilliant cut, delivering strong face up scintillation while preserving color saturation. The length to width ratios are approximately 1.28 and 1.25, providing an elegant oval outline that reads slightly elongated on the finger but remains balanced for pendants and stud settings. Average diameters are 7.81 millimeters and 7.905 millimeters, which yield depth proportions of approximately 53.5 percent and 54.6 percent respectively, values that fall within an optimal window for both light return and preservation of the intense greenish blue hue. Clarity is graded as very very slightly included at eye level, a level of internal cleanliness that allows exceptional transparency and brilliance without visible obstruction to the wearer, and the polish is graded excellent, indicating a mirror like facet finish and very crisp facet junctions.

The mixed brilliant faceting has been executed to emphasize color and smooth finish, combining a modified brilliant crown with a precision faceted pavilion that enhances internal reflection while reducing windowing. Crown facet angles and pavilion relationships have been balanced to optimize both sparkle and color saturation, with the table sizes chosen to present a vivid face up appearance under typical lighting conditions. Facet junctions are tight and well aligned, producing continuous light return and contributing to a glass like smoothness across each curvature. The girdles have been finished to a consistent thin to medium thickness to allow secure bezel or prong settings without visible overhang, and the culets are small and centered to support symmetrical performance. The excellent polish is the result of controlled mechanical finishing followed by hand lap polishing using progressively finer abrasives and a final high quality diamond paste pass, procedures that minimize micro abrasions and produce the smooth finish that high end designers require for seamless metal integration.

These gemstones are heat treated to stabilize and intensify the greenish blue tone, a standard enhancement for apatite that is permanent under normal wear but should be considered during jewelry fabrication and care. Given apatite hardness near five on the Mohs scale and its brittle cleavage tendency, recommended design approaches include protective settings such as low profile bezel mounts, partially filled bezels, or well executed prong work with secure gallery support, designs that preserve the stones smooth finish and mitigate impact risk. For metal selection, 18 karat white gold or platinum will emphasize the cooler blue facets and the gem s brilliance, while 18 karat yellow gold will subtly warm the green component of the hue, allowing tailored color interaction in custom pieces. This pair is particularly appropriate for matched stud earrings or a complementary pendant and ring set, where the matched dimensions and symmetry will provide a cohesive face up presentation. For sourcing, matching, and bespoke mounting services please consult The Natural Gemstone Company, our team can provide additional imagery under directional light, recommendation on setting architecture that preserves the smooth finish, and guidance on cleaning that relies on mild soapy water and a soft brush rather than steam or aggressive ultrasonic treatments to maintain the integrity of the polish and the stability of the heat treatment.

Measuring 15.03 by 10.85 by 8.05 millimeters, the stone is expertly fashioned into a smooth cabochon that showcases its natural bi-color transition from lemon yellow to fresh green, with a medium color intensity that reads vibrantly in daylight. Evaluated at eye level, clarity is slightly included, a characteristic that adds character rather than distraction, and the excellent polish enhances the stone's soft glow and tactile appeal. This fluorite is completely natural with no enhancements, making it a pure expression of its Sri Lankan origin. For customers who treasure complementary pairings, consider combining this piece with a White Opal accent, the cool opalescence of White Opal harmonizing beautifully with the fluorite's two-tone personality to create rings, pendants, or bespoke pieces that feel both gentle and distinctive. The Natural Gemstone Company presents this gem as an ideal choice for a unique engagement ring, a statement cabochon for bespoke jewelry, or a standout addition to a collector's cabinet, satisfying desires for rarity, hand-worthy size, and authentic provenance.

Unlike more commonly seen gemstones that rely on faceted fire or high refractive index for brilliance, this bi-color fluorite offers a different kind of radiance, an inner luminosity that feels alive and intimate. Where diamonds and sapphires dazzle with scintillation and topaz or aquamarine flash with clearer, faceted brightness, the fluorite's cabochon cut softens light into a luminous wash that emphasizes color zoning and depth rather than sparkle. The result is a stone that stands out in a collection because it invites touch and contemplation, revealing subtle shifts in tone as the hand moves and the light changes. Its translucence and excellent polish create a silky sheen that complements gold or silver settings and pairs especially well with the milky, play-of-color of White Opal for designs that are refined, unusual, and emotionally resonant. If your need is a gem that reads as singular and soulful rather than simply brilliant, this Ceylon bi-color fluorite from The Natural Gemstone Company fulfills that desire with authenticity, presence, and a quiet, unforgettable glow.

At The Natural Gemstone Company we recognize that shopping for a gemstone often feels like a final search for the right piece of the puzzle. title: K12338
descriptionHtml:
This listing describes a single, transparent purplish pink kunzite weighing 15.73 carats, presented in a cushion shape, with precise dimensions of 16.58 x 13.46 x 9.15 mm, prepared by skilled lapidary work. The cutting style is faceted, executed as a mixed brilliant cut, combining pavilion facets that enhance brilliance with a crown arrangement that maximizes color and windowing control. Clarity is graded as eye clean, evaluated at eye level, indicating the absence of inclusions visible without magnification, and the surface finish is characterized by an excellent polish. The color is a medium intensity purplish pink, offering a balanced saturation that reads vividly in a variety of lighting conditions without appearing overly dark. The material has been heat treated to enhance and stabilize the hue, consistent with common, accepted enhancement practices for this variety, and the piece originates from Madagascar, a recognized source of fine gem quality kunzite.

Optical and material attributes of this kunzite are important for assessment and design considerations, the stone is transparent with a clean window through the table, and the mixed brilliant faceting promotes lively return of light while shaping the apparent face color. Pleochroism is a known characteristic of kunzite, and this stone displays subtle directional color variations when viewed from different angles, which can add depth and visual interest in finished jewelry. The excellent polish supports optimal light performance and tactile smoothness, contributing to a refined appearance when set. The cushion outline is a versatile choice that can be used in a range of mounting styles, from classic solitaire settings to more elaborate designs that emphasize the stone as the focal point. Because the clarity is eye clean, the faceting pattern can be appreciated without distraction from internal features, supporting both aesthetic quality and valuation.

On the Mohs scale of mineral hardness, kunzite registers at approximately 6.5 to 7, this places it below traditionally durable stones such as sapphire at 9 and topaz at 8, and at or slightly below common quartz at 7. The hardness indicates reasonable resistance to abrasion during normal wear, however this should be considered in the context of the mineral’s crystallographic properties, kunzite is a member of the spodumene group and exhibits distinct cleavage in two directions, this pronounced cleavage makes it more susceptible to fracture or splitting if struck or subjected to lateral pressure. For practical durability and long term care, settings that provide protective bezels or deep prongs, and designs that shield the girdle and edges are recommended, because even with a surface that resists scratches to a degree, impact or sharp blows can propagate along cleavage planes more readily than in isotropic or tougher gem materials.

Care and handling guidance is provided to preserve both color and structural integrity, avoid exposure to prolonged high heat or intense sunlight for extended periods because kunzite can be sensitive to light and may gradually fade if left under direct sunlight for very long durations, the heat treated enhancement applied to this stone is stable under normal wearing conditions, however extreme heat can risk alteration. Ultrasonic and steam cleaning are not recommended without prior consultation with a qualified gemologist, gentle cleaning with warm soapy water and a soft brush is the preferred method. For settings, choose designs that minimize exposure of the stone’s edges while allowing light to interact with the crown, this approach maintains aesthetic appeal while mitigating the risk associated with cleavage. The Natural Gemstone Company stands behind the accuracy of the description and the provenance information, and can provide additional documentation regarding treatment and origin upon request, the provided details assist in responsible selection for collectors, designers, and end users who prioritize a balance of visual quality and practical considerations in handling and wearing.

title: PR12858
descriptionHtml:
The Natural Gemstone Company presents an exceptional matched pair of oval pink kunzites, each expertly cut and polished for high end jewelry creation. These stones weigh 7.09 carats and 7.16 carats respectively, and their substantial sizes are complemented by well balanced proportions, with dimensions of 12.30 x 10.29 x 7.86 mm and 12.34 x 10.28 x 7.90 mm. Both gems are fashioned in a mixed brilliant cut, a choice that combines a brilliant style crown with a faceted pavilion to harmonize scintillation and depth. The color is described as medium intensity pink, a tone that reads as elegant and wearable while retaining good saturation for presence in finished pieces. Enhancement is by heat treatment, a stable and widely accepted method used to refine hue and reduce undesirable undertones, and the origin of these stones is Afghanistan, a source known for producing attractive pink spodumene specimens.

From a gemological perspective these kunzites offer a compelling combination of optical performance and clarity. The mixed brilliant cut enhances return of light through a carefully considered balance of facet angles, yielding lively scintillation on the table and controlled light return through the pavilion for visual depth. Clarity is graded very very slightly included, evaluated at eye level, which for most practical purposes translates to eye clean appearance, with only minute internal features detectable under magnification. This clarity grade allows the pink color to remain pure and unobstructed, and the excellent polish contributes to a smooth finish that enhances surface luster and tactile quality. The overall smooth finish is especially important for high end designs because it reduces the need for aggressive metalwork finishing, ensures comfortable wear against the skin, and presents crisp facet junctions that read clearly under jeweler magnification and to an informed buyer.

Kunzite is a gem variety of spodumene, a lithium aluminum silicate, and it is known for its delicate pink to violet hues and for displaying strong pleochroism, where color can vary with crystal orientation. For this reason, precise cutting and matching are critical for a paired set intended for earrings or symmetrical designs. The cutters of these stones elected a mixed brilliant approach and aligned the orientation to maximize face up color and to control the pleochroic behavior, producing a balanced pair where color tone and bodycolor are closely matched. The near equality of weight and dimensions in this pair is notable, and it simplifies the design process when fabricating matched earrings or a two stone pendant, because the stones will sit consistently and reflect light in a uniform manner. Sourcing from Afghanistan adds provenance that educated buyers appreciate, as this origin is associated with well colored and well crystallized kunzite specimens, making this pair desirable for collectors and designers who value traceable supply and documented treatment.

For design considerations these kunzites are particularly well suited to high end settings where a smooth finish and excellent polish will be showcased. They work beautifully in classic prong settings that allow maximum light entry, in bezel settings for a contemporary, clean aesthetic where the smooth girdle and polish will meet the metal elegantly, and in halo compositions where the medium intensity pink will pop against diamonds or other colorless accent stones. Because the stones are closely matched in weight and proportion, they are ideal for precision matched earrings, or for bespoke two stone pieces that require symmetry. The heat treatment applied to refine hue is stable under normal wear, and the very very slightly included clarity grade means the stones will photograph cleanly and perform reliably under close inspection. The Natural Gemstone Company stands behind the descriptive details provided, and we welcome inquiries from designers and collectors seeking additional information such as facet diagrams, viewing angles, or setting recommendations to ensure the final piece achieves the highest level of craftsmanship and visual harmony.

title: K17557
descriptionHtml:
This translucent multi color onyx presents as a substantial 17.18 carat oval cabochon, precisely measured at 19.49 x 14.44 x 7.29 millimeters, exhibiting a clean, symmetrical outline and an even domed profile that optimizes face up color and internal structure. The cabochon cut is executed to exacting lapidary standards, with a centrally placed apex, calibrated dome curvature to balance light transmission and surface reflection, and a consistent girdle thickness that facilitates secure mounting. The surface retains an excellent polish, achieved through progressive micron grade abrasives, which yields a smooth vitreous to slightly waxy luster appropriate to cryptocrystalline chalcedony. There are no treatments or enhancements, the material is wholly natural, and the piece is sourced from Madagascar, a region noted for producing high quality chalcedony variants with complex color zoning.

From a gemological perspective this onyx sits within the chalcedony group, chemically SiO2, with a refractive index typically near 1.53 to 1.54 and a specific gravity in the region of 2.60 to 2.64, characteristics that confirm its silica based, cryptocrystalline structure. The designation color intensity not applicable reflects the multi tonal nature of the piece rather than a single saturated hue, and under transmitted and reflected light the material displays layered color transitions and subdued internal banding that provide visual depth without strong pleochroism. The absence of macroscopic cleavage combined with the fine interlocking fibrous microstructure contributes to consistent toughness, while the translucent body allows subtle internal patterning to read clearly through the domed surface, enhancing the perceived size and presence of the stone.

Durability attributes make this onyx an excellent candidate for daily wear jewelry, provided appropriate settings and routine care are observed. On the Mohs scale the material registers approximately 6.5 to 7, offering strong resistance to abrasion from many common contacts while remaining softer than corundum and diamond class stones, so care should be taken to avoid scraping against harder materials. The cabochon profile reduces the risk of perimeter chipping relative to faceted sharp edges, and the excellent polish minimizes surface micro abrasions that would otherwise diminish translucency over time. The material is stable to ordinary light exposure and normal thermal conditions encountered in daily use, however it is prudent to avoid prolonged exposure to strong acids and harsh industrial chemicals. For cleaning we recommend warm soapy water and a soft brush, with ultrasonic and steam cleaning reserved for evaluation by a professional when mounting and setting details are known.

For secure everyday mounting a bezel setting is recommended to protect the cabochon rim and distribute impact stress across the girdle, however a well designed prong setting with protective crowns or a partial bezel can also provide both security and maximum face up display. The dimensions and weight of this oval make it particularly suitable for statement rings, pendants, or masculine cufflinks where the substantial face enhances color play and presence. The provenance from Madagascar, coupled with the lack of enhancement, positions this piece as a collectible natural specimen with stable long term performance. The Natural Gemstone Company stands behind the craftsmanship and disclosure of this onyx, and we can provide additional technical documentation or bespoke mounting recommendations to ensure optimal durability and aesthetics for everyday wear.

title: K12034
descriptionHtml:
This exquisite opaque 0.19 carat round salmon orange coral is presented as a classic cabochon, with precise dimensions of 3.95 by 3.98 by 1.87 millimeters. The rounded dome and symmetrical outline speak to careful lapidary work, and the vivid color intensity that this specimen exhibits is immediately eye catching. Cabochon cutting is the traditional style for natural corals, and the smooth domed surface of this piece maximizes the saturation and visual depth of the salmon orange hue. The finish on this gem is of excellent polish, producing a refined satiny gleam that highlights the coral grain and subtle internal structure. This item is unenhanced, remaining in its natural state with no dyeing, bleaching, or resin treatments, and it is documented as originating from Italy, a region renowned for its historical supply of Mediterranean corals and long established craftsmanship in coral cutting and jewelry.

From a collector and connoisseur perspective the key grading factors for this coral are color intensity, surface condition, symmetry, and treatment status, and this specimen scores strongly across each of those attributes. The color is vivid rather than pastel, placing it in a premium category for salmon and orange toned corals where saturation and uniformity matter most. Although coral is an organic material and not graded by traditional clarity scales used for minerals, clarity for coral is evaluated in terms of surface blemishes, porosity, and visible growth structures. This cabochon is free from major surface pits or disruptive fractures, and the polish has been executed to reduce the appearance of any minor textural features, resulting in a clean visual field that allows the natural grain to be appreciated without distraction. The round shape is well centered and the measurements confirm a compact high precision piece, which will sit evenly in a bezel or prong setting, lending itself to secure mounting and elegant presentation.

The provenance of Italian coral lends further significance to the piece, especially for educated buyers who place value on origin and authenticity. Mediterranean corals from Italy carry a storied cultural history and were historically used in high end European jewelry, making specimens from this region desirable for curated collections that emphasize provenance and heritage. In addition, coral harvesting in many maritime regions is now subject to regulation and quota systems, which has limited supply and increased the scarcity and collectible value of quality untreated material. Because this coral is natural and unenhanced, it retains the original material characteristics that serious collectors and designers prefer, making it suitable for museum quality pieces, bespoke high end commissions, and refined jewelry collections. The modest 0.19 carat weight does not diminish its desirability, since collectors often prize specimens for color purity and origin rather than sheer size, and small well formed cabochons like this one are particularly valuable for precision inlay work, fine cluster designs, and for pairing with other gemstones to create balanced color compositions.

Practical considerations for integrating this coral into a high end gemstone collection include suggestions for mounting, conservation, and authentication. As an organic gem, coral benefits from settings that protect it from sharp impacts and prolonged exposure to acids, chemicals, and extreme heat, so bezel settings and protective design elements are recommended. The cabochon dome should be oriented to showcase the most uniform color face and to minimize the visibility of any minor growth lines. For long term preservation, gentle cleaning with a soft cloth and mild soapy water is preferred, and avoidance of ultrasonic cleaners and harsh detergents will prolong the surface polish. For buyers who require verification and trust, The Natural Gemstone Company stands behind the origin and non enhanced status of this coral and can provide detailed imagery, measurements, and provenance notes on request, supporting confident acquisition and seamless integration into an existing collection. With its vivid salmon orange tone, excellent polish, symmetrical round cabochon form, and documented Italian origin, this coral is an ideal addition to a discerning high end gemstone collection.

descriptionHtml:
One beautiful opaque 9.60 carat cushion shape blue lapis with dimensions 14.02 x 12.04 x 6.27 mm arrives to you with a cabochon cut and an excellent polish, and it carries the unmistakable deep blue presence that has been prized for millennia. This stone is entirely natural, with no enhancement, and its origin in Afghanistan places it among the most respected and historically significant sources of lapis lazuli. The cushion outline has been carefully shaped to balance presence and wearability, and the cabochon dome allows the rich, opaque color to sing across the surface while the excellent polish produces a soft, luminous sheen rather than a mirror like glare. At 9.60 carats this lapis has substantial size without overwhelming a setting, and the measurements 14.02 x 12.04 x 6.27 mm make it ideal for a bold ring, a pendant centerpiece, or a custom brooch. The Natural Gemstone Company is proud to present this Afghan lapis as a single, honest example of what untreated lapis can offer, combining traditional character with modern finishing standards.

When comparing this lapis to famous gemstones in history, it is useful to consider different kinds of fame and function. The Hope Diamond thrilled the world with its size, clarity, and brilliant faceting, it is a lesson in how light plays through a transparent crystal. This lapis offers a different kind of historic resonance, one more akin to the lapis panels in ancient Mesopotamian and Egyptian art, and to the ultramarine pigment derived from lapis that Renaissance masters used in their most revered paintings. Where a sapphire like the Star of India or a Koh i Noor impressed with hardness and high refractive brilliance, this Afghan lapis stands out for its opaque, painterly color and cultural lineage. In historic jewelry lapis has been used as symbolic blue in crowns, amulets, and sacred objects, and the present cabochon form echoes those antique uses. The golden pyrite specks that may appear in lapis are like tiny stars embedded in stone, a visual attribute that no transparent corundum can replicate. Choosing this piece therefore means owning a gem that aligns with art history and ancient prestige, rather than pursuing brilliance alone.

In comparing quality and value to other market options, this stone has clear advantages. Many commercially available blue stones are either transparent corundums, treated or dyed materials, or synthetics that aim to mimic the lapis tone. This lapis is untreated and originates from Afghanistan, a region renowned for producing the deepest, most saturated lapis material, which makes it inherently more collectible and desirable than stabilized or dyed alternatives. The cabochon cut and cushion shape maximize the depth of color while minimizing the visibility of any internal structure, and the excellent polish ensures that the surface reads uniformly in various light conditions. For designers and collectors who seek authenticity, the no enhancement attribute dramatically increases long term value and trust. The weight and size allow for a variety of design possibilities, and the stone pairs particularly well with warm metals like 18 karat yellow gold where the blue and gold tones resonate with the pyrite flecks, though it also works beautifully with vintage white metals when set in more subdued, museum style settings. Versus popular imitations such as dyed howlite or low grade sodalite, this natural lapis offers a richer color saturation, a healthier surface polish, and a storied provenance that adds narrative to every piece of jewelry made from it.

The Natural Gemstone Company stands behind the sourcing and presentation of this Afghan lapis, and we emphasize provenance, honesty, and long term value in every offering. For collectors who value historical continuity, this piece connects to the same mineral lineage that produced the ultramarine pigments of the great painters and the lapis in ancient ceremonial objects. For the designer seeking a statement cabochon that will age gracefully and remain visually compelling, the 9.60 carat size and the cushion proportions are both practical and striking. Care is straightforward, avoid harsh chemicals and prolonged exposure to acids or abrasive cleaners, and clean gently with a soft cloth and mild soapy water when needed, avoid ultrasonic cleaning to preserve the surface and polish. If you require additional images, setting suggestions, or information about matching stones for a pair, The Natural Gemstone Company is prepared to assist with custom options and with certification of origin. This Afghan lapis is a rare opportunity to acquire an untreated, excellently finished example of an ancient and beloved material, a stone that brings both historical resonance and contemporary design potential to any collection.

This listing presents one opaque blue turquoise cabochon weighing 27.74 carats, round in outline, with precise dimensions of 17.44 by 17.53 by 12.15 millimeters, cabochon cut, medium color intensity, excellent polish, no enhancement, origin United States, offered by The Natural Gemstone Company. The carat weight and dimensional data indicate a substantial example suitable for high profile settings, and the nearly perfect round outline reflects careful preforming and trimming during the cutting process. The designation of opaque reflects the internal structure and light behavior typical of turquoise, and the absence of enhancements confirms that the color and stability are inherent to the material as extracted. The combination of size and natural color without stabilization or dye places this specimen in a distinct category for collectors and designers who prioritize untreated American turquoise.

Color evaluation for this stone falls into the medium intensity band, with a primary hue in the sky blue to robin egg blue range, uniform across the dome with minimal visible matrix or veining. Under standard daylight equivalent illumination the stone exhibits even color distribution, with subtle surface luster derived from the polish rather than any translucency. The spectral and visual response is consistent with turquoise mineralogy, which typically displays refractive indices in the 1.61 to 1.65 range, and specific gravity commonly near 2.6 to 2.9, values that this cabochon conforms to when measured with standard gemological tools. The color saturation is balanced, neither washed nor overly deep, which aids in versatility when pairing with different metal tones and accent gems, and the medium intensity provides a pleasing visual impact without overpowering delicate design elements.

The cabochon execution demonstrates advanced lapidary technique, with a high domed profile of 12.15 millimeters that enhances color depth and provides a pleasing bulk for bezel mounting. The cutter preserved the natural surface continuity, using progressive grit stages to remove saw and grind marks, followed by fine lap polishing likely with tin oxide or cerium oxide to achieve the excellent polish reported. Edge control is precise, the girdle is consistent and free of nicks or chips, and the dome symmetry across the 17.44 and 17.53 millimeter axes is within typical tolerances for hand cutting, indicating careful control of preform rotation and lap pressure. The absence of stabilization treatments means that all cutting decisions were made to conserve thickness and avoid exposing sensitive zones, while still presenting an even convex platform that will sit securely in a bezel or collet setting.

From a provenance and use perspective the American origin adds both market recognition and collector interest, as natural US turquoise is often sought after for its historical and gemological significance. At 27.74 carats and with dimensions that allow for prominent placement, this cabochon is ideal for bespoke rings, statement pendants, and museum quality pieces, particularly when set to protect the stone from abrasion given turquoise hardness in the lower mid range. Recommended mounting approaches include full bezel seats to guard the girdle and sides, or three quarter bezels combined with protective crowns to reduce impact exposure, and practitioners should avoid high tension settings that place point stress on the body of the cabochon. Care instructions include gentle cleaning with a soft cloth and mild soap and water, avoidance of acids, solvents, and ultrasonic or steam cleaners, and storage away from prolonged heat and chemical contact to preserve the natural color and surface integrity. For professional inquiries and to view additional documentation on this untreated American turquoise please contact The Natural Gemstone Company, we can provide gemological data, handling advice, and custom setting recommendations tailored to this particular 27.74 carat blue turquoise.
