title: K12523
descriptionHtml:
From the slow patience of the earth to the calm certainty of the jeweler s hand this blue turquoise began its life in the arid folds of the American landscape where copper rich waters quietly altered host rocks over millennia, depositing the delicate bluish green that we now call turquoise. Mined in the United States this specimen is an opaque round cabochon weighing 9.84 carats with dimensions 13.44 x 13.25 x 7.70 mm, medium color intensity, an excellent polish, and no enhancement. Each curve and belly of the cabochon retains the memory of rock, weather, and time, and here at The Natural Gemstone Company we honor that memory by letting the natural surface and tone lead the cutting and finishing decisions. This gem arrived in our studio as a rough of modest size and disciplined color, and our lapidary chose a round shape to emphasize its even color spread and pleasing symmetry, a choice that preserves both the stone s natural character and its potential to sit serenely in a ring, pendant, or pair of earrings.

The cabochon cut softens light across the stone s face and reveals a medium blue that sits between sky and sea, a hue that is quietly assertive rather than loudly brilliant. Compared to Persian turquoise from Iran with its classic intense sky blue and often glassy saturation, this American stone leans slightly toward a more approachable, medium intensity blue that carries a grounded, earthy tone. Compared to the famed Sleeping Beauty mines in Arizona, which yield stones known for an iconic robin s egg blue and often needle clear purity, this turquoise offers a warmer and more muted temperament, with a depth that invites close inspection. Compared to Nevada and New Mexico varieties that can swing greener or display pronounced matrix and tonal complexity, this round cabochon is more consistently blue, lacking prominent veins, which allows a single, calm hue to dominate. Compared to ancient Egyptian Sinai turquoise which tends to show softer greenish tones and a less saturated finish, the American piece at hand maintains a cleaner blue leaning, a pleasing middle ground that many buyers find versatile and wearable. These comparisons help situate the gem s personality, showing it as a balanced American turquoise that sits comfortably between the high sky blues of Persian stones and the greener, more matrixed varieties of other localities.

The journey from rough to polished cabochon is a narrative of restraint and respect, where every decision is made to highlight what nature already offered. Our lapidaries removed distractions, smoothed the cabochon s dome, and achieved an excellent polish that allows touch to feel the stone s history and light to reveal its inner color without artificial enhancement. No dyeing, stabilization, or resin infill has been applied, so the gem will patina and age like any natural turquoise when worn, deepening in character with time and contact with the wearer. In terms of tone the piece offers medium saturation, which means it is neither the spectral blue of high grade Persian turquoise nor the deep teal of some mined in arid basins, but rather a versatile blue that pairs beautifully with warm metals like gold and with silver, complementing traditional Southwestern designs as well as contemporary minimalist settings. For those who treasure provenance the American origin carries cultural resonance, linking the piece to the craft traditions of the Southwest, and when set into jewelry it becomes part of a living story of place, hands, and meaning.

As a wearable artifact this 9.84 carat round cabochon makes a confident center stone for a statement ring, a refined focal point for a pendant, or a singular gem for a bespoke brooch, its medium blue providing a comfortable middle ground for everyday wear or for special occasions. Care is straightforward, avoid harsh chemicals and prolonged soaking, wipe with a soft cloth after wear, and store it separately to keep that excellent polish pristine. At The Natural Gemstone Company we are proud to present gemstones that tell their origin story honestly and beautifully, and this American turquoise is a fine example of a gem whose hue and tone honor a specific landscape while remaining adaptable to many styles. If you would like a closer look at photos, or wish to discuss setting options or custom design, we are ready to share the next chapters of this turquoise s journey, from our hands into yours.

title: K17948
descriptionHtml:
This transparent 1.08 carat emerald cut green andradite garnet from Russia presents a refined balance of color, clarity, and cut that stands out among green gemstones on the market, and The Natural Gemstone Company is proud to offer this stone to discerning buyers. The stone measures 6.30 by 4.79 by 3.86 mm, and its emerald cut delivers crisp step facets and a broad table that emphasizes the medium intense green color, while the excellent polish maximizes light return and surface smoothness. At a clarity grade of slightly included, evaluated at eye level, the inclusions are minor and do not detract from the gem’s overall transparency or brilliance. Compared to commercial peridot and many green tourmalines, which can show lighter tones or uneven color distribution, this green andradite displays a richer and more stable medium intense hue that reads as sophisticated in both daylight and artificial lighting. Compared to emerald, which is often treated with oils and has more prominent internal fissures making it fragile for everyday wear, andradite offers a more robust option with fewer tradeoffs in visual appeal.

When evaluating daily wear suitability, both hardness and toughness matter, and this green andradite garnet performs very well for regular use in jewelry. Andradite garnets typically fall in the mid to upper range of the Mohs hardness scale near 6.5 to 7.5, and they have no perfect cleavage, which reduces the risk of splitting under impact. The heat treatment applied to this stone is a standard enhancement intended to stabilize and enrich the green tone, and this treatment is permanent under normal wear conditions, meaning the color will not fade with exposure to sunlight or the gentle cleaning agents used at home. The emerald cut with its stepped pavilion and carefully finished girdle also contributes to durability, as the geometry reduces points and thin edges that commonly chip, and the excellent polish minimizes microabrasions that would otherwise dull the surface over time. For customers comparing value, this gem offers a rare combination of a clean, transparent appearance and strong color saturation, at a price point that undercuts comparable rare green stones such as tsavorite and demantoid, while delivering superior durability to emeralds and greater color stability than many green tourmalines.

Practical guidance for setting and long term care enhances the daily wear benefits of this stone, and The Natural Gemstone Company recommends settings that further protect the stone without obscuring its allure. A bezel setting or a four prong setting with reinforced or rounded corners is ideal for an emerald cut stone, as these approaches protect the girdle and corners while allowing the table and step facets to present their full brilliance. Routine care can be simple, using mild soap and warm water, and avoiding harsh ultrasonic cleaning if the mounting or enamels could be affected, although the heat treatment itself does not make the stone more vulnerable to normal household cleaning. Compared to high hardness but brittle gems like topaz, which can cleave, and very soft gems like opal, which risk abrasion, this green andradite garnet presents an excellent middle ground for everyday rings, pendants, and even daily wear earrings, offering both resilience and enduring visual appeal. When you choose this gemstone from The Natural Gemstone Company, you are selecting a Russian origin andradite with a unique, medium intense green, strong polish, secure clarity, and practical durability that makes it an excellent choice for jewelry you intend to wear every day.

descriptionHtml:
This pear shaped carnelian presents as a translucent, well proportioned gem with a precise weight of 5.82 carat and dimensions of 14.00 x 10.16 x 5.78 mm, reflecting careful selection and cutting. The stone is fashioned as a cabochon, an approach that emphasizes its smooth domed profile and allows the internal color to be viewed uninterrupted. The hue registers as a reddish orange with medium color intensity, offering a warm and uniform saturation across the surface. The polish is excellent, resulting in a high degree of surface luster and soft reflective highlights that move smoothly over the dome. The material is dye treated, an enhancement that has been applied to enrich the base color and to achieve even tonal distribution. Origin is Brazil, a notable source for quality chalcedony varieties, and this provenance is consistent with the structural and textural characteristics evident in the stone. For comparative reference within our inventory, we also note the availability of opal material described as White Opal, also known as Light Opal, which displays its own distinct body tone and optical character, and may be considered when planning paired or contrasted designs with this carnelian.

The formation narrative of this carnelian spans deep geological time, rooted in processes that unfolded over millions of years. Carnelian is a variety of microcrystalline quartz that developed from silica rich solutions which migrated through volcanic and sedimentary rock structures. In the depositional environment typical of Brazilian sources, silica laden fluids permeated cavities and pore spaces, often filling voids within ancient lavas or sedimentary layers. As the silica gel gradually solidified and recrystallized at low temperatures, microscopic quartz crystals arranged themselves into the compact, fibrous chalcedony texture characteristic of carnelian. Trace amounts of iron oxides became incorporated during or after this crystallization, imparting the reddish orange color that defines the specimen. Over extended geological timeframes, subsequent burial and subtle thermal and chemical alteration contributed to the stabilization and consolidation of the material. The cabochon cut selected for this piece follows the stone through its history, presenting the compact internal structure as a smooth surface that reveals translucency and depth rather than facet derived brilliance.

In practical terms this carnelian combines aesthetic and material properties that are relevant to both gem professionals and discerning clients. At a hardness near 6.5 to 7 on the Mohs scale, the stone offers a durable option for a variety of jewelry settings, particularly for pieces where the cabochon form can be secured within bezels or partial bezels to protect the perimeter. The medium intensity and uniform saturation are well suited to designs that prioritize color harmony, and the translucency allows light to pass and diffuse through the dome, creating a warm internal glow. The dye treatment should be considered when specifying long term care and potential exposure to strong solvents or prolonged heat, and standard precautions for dyed chalcedony are advised. When juxtaposing this carnelian with White Opal Light Opal, note that the opal will present a fundamentally different optical profile and care requirement, offering contrast in body tone and play of light. The Natural Gemstone Company provides this piece with full disclosure of treatment and origin, and we include measurements and photographic representation to support accurate assessment for design and appraisal purposes. This description aims to present the factual and geological context of the gem, along with its physical and optical attributes, to assist professional and private clients in making a considered evaluation.

title: K11397
descriptionHtml:
This gemstone is a transparent orange hessonite garnet, weighing 3.20 carat, presenting an oval outline with dimensions of 8.91 x 7.70 x 6.12 mm. The cutter selected a mixed brilliant cut to balance light performance and color depth, resulting in lively scintillation and a well defined silhouette. Clarity is graded as slightly included, evaluated at eye level, which affirms that the stone displays natural inclusions without compromising visual appeal. Color intensity is vivid, and polish is excellent, enabling crisp facet junctions and a smooth, reflective surface. No enhancement has been applied to alter color or clarity, and the material is sourced from Madagascar, a region known for producing hessonite with warm, honeyed to orange tones. These objective attributes are recorded to provide a clear account of the gem as it arrives into the inventory of The Natural Gemstone Company.

The journey of this hessonite begins in a deposit in Madagascar where artisanal and small scale mining operations work within seasonal patterns dictated by weather and terrain. Experienced local teams extract pockets of gem bearing matrix, paying attention to the geological context that produces hessonite. From the moment the crystal emerges, a sequence of manual inspections separates gem quality fragments from lower grade material, and the rough destined for further processing is transported to a regional hub for initial trimming and stabilization. Along the route the material is recorded and packed to preserve traceability, and local handlers document origin and source conditions to support responsible sourcing. This stage is deliberate and methodical, emphasizing the continuity from extraction to eventual market offering, and it establishes the provenance that underpins subsequent grading and presentation.

Once the rough reaches the cutting atelier, the stone is examined under controlled lighting to assess color orientation, inclusion placement, and the most advantageous cutting strategy. The decision to execute a mixed brilliant cut was informed by the need to retain weight while maximizing face up color and brilliance. The cutter mapped the crystal, identifying the plane that would yield the most balanced oval outline and planned pavilion and crown angles to enhance return of light. During faceting, slight inclusions were consciously positioned to remain unobtrusive to the naked eye, and feathering of facets was minimized to maintain visual integrity. Polish was executed with fine abrasives and progressive laps to achieve a mirror like finish. Throughout these steps measurements were recorded, and the final dimensions 8.91 x 7.70 x 6.12 mm and weight 3.20 carat were verified. A final evaluation confirmed vivid color intensity, excellent polish, and the clarity grade slightly included, all while affirming that no enhancement was applied to the stone.

Upon completion of cutting and grading, the gem entered quality control and inventory under the stewardship of The Natural Gemstone Company. Each attribute was documented to provide a transparent record for clients and for responsible retail presentation. Accompanying notes describe the Madagascar origin, the lack of enhancement, and the precise technical specifications including weight, shape, cut style, clarity assessment, color intensity, and polish quality. Handling and storage follow protocols that protect the polish and prevent abrasion, and recommendations for care are provided to maintain the stone in its present condition. For jewelry integration, the mixed brilliant faceting and oval proportions make this hessonite suitable for a variety of settings where secure mounting and protective design preserve the girdle and thickness. The narrative from mine to market is intended to offer a clear and factual account of the gemstone lifecycle, preserving both the scientific details that inform valuation and the human elements that document ethical sourcing and craftsmanship.

descriptionHtml:
This pair of Other certified Blue cobalt spinels from Tanzania arrives as a rare duet of pure, crystalline color, a true statement of exclusivity reserved for those who seek something beyond the ordinary. Weighing 0.99 carats and 1.08 carats respectively, and cut into elegant ovals with dimensions of 6.64 x 5.48 x 3.75 mm and 6.72 x 5.45 x 3.66 mm, these gems present as a perfectly matched pair for a bespoke set of earrings or a matched jewelry commission. Each stone bears a mixed brilliant cut that has been executed with precision to maximize both color saturation and scintillation, and the excellent polish reveals a surface so smooth and reflective that light plays across each facet with a lively, energetic sparkle. The clarity grade is evaluated as very very slightly included at eye level, indicating that to the naked eye these spinels appear clean and uninterrupted, a visual purity that elevates any piece they adorn. Most importantly, these stones have no enhancement, an increasingly uncommon attribute in the marketplace, which means the vivid intensity you see is entirely natural, a rare occurrence that places these pieces in a category of their own, and this authentic rarity comes to you through The Natural Gemstone Company.

When you compare the brilliance of these cobalt spinels to more common blue gemstones the difference is immediately perceptible. A sapphire in a similar hue may be admired for its depth, but many fine blue sapphires undergo heat treatment, and some carry a subtle veil of rutile or silk inclusions that diffuse light, softening sparkle. Aquamarine and blue topaz are frequently paler and more watery, trading saturated color for a cool, restrained tone, and in many cases they lack the intensity that makes a deep blue truly commanding. Diamond offers unmatched fire and brilliance, but it does so in the absence of color, and the experience of a vivid blue is an entirely different kind of luxury. Cobalt spinel sits apart because it combines a pure, vivid blue chroma with an optical performance that returns light in quick, bright flashes. The mixed brilliant cut enhances that effect by creating a balanced interplay between large facets for color and small facets for scintillation, so the result is a gem that appears both deeply colored and vividly alive, a quality that is rare among blue gemstones and deeply prized by connoisseurs.

The provenance of these pieces further enhances their desirability, as Tanzania has proven itself a source of some of the most notable cobalt spinels discovered in recent years. The combination of geographic origin, natural vivid color intensity, and the absence of any enhancement creates a story of geological fortune and human stewardship, a story you carry when you choose to wear these gems. In practical terms this means you are investing in a pair that will retain its visual identity without the complications of treatments that can alter over time. The excellent polish and precise mixed brilliant cut ensure that these stones sit beautifully in light, maintaining a steady, spirited brilliance whether viewed in daylight or by evening illumination. For someone who appreciates the finer nuances of color and light, owning untreated cobalt spinel of this caliber is akin to possessing a signature hue that cannot be reproduced by common heat treatments or irradiations.

To choose this pair from The Natural Gemstone Company is to join an exclusive circle of collectors and designers who understand that true rarity is not only about weight or size, but about provenance, natural color, and the integrity of the gem itself. These spinels offer a canvas for bespoke design, lending themselves to classic settings that let their vivid blue sing, or to modern designs that emphasize color and purity. The matched nature of the pair means symmetry and balance for a finished piece, and the very very slightly included clarity ensures eye clean presentation while preserving a natural story within each crystal. Opportunities to acquire naturally vivid, untreated cobalt spinel of this precision are limited, and when matched pairs appear on the market they are often claimed swiftly by those who recognize their scarcity. If you seek a gemstone that stands apart from the familiar blue stones of mainstream jewelry, and if you value authenticity, provenance, and exceptional optical performance, these two cobalt spinels represent a rare chance to own something genuinely singular, presented with the assurance and expertise of The Natural Gemstone Company.

title: K12039
descriptionHtml:
One beautiful transparent 10.34 carat radiant shape white jeremejevite with dimensions of 12.84 x 11.23 x 9.17 mm is available through The Natural Gemstone Company, and this stone presents a rare opportunity for a discerning collector or connoisseur of fine gems. The radiant cut combines the elegant rectangular outline with trimmed corners and a faceting scheme that maximizes light return for stones with slightly different crystal habits. This particular jeremejevite is colorless in intensity, offering a pure, crystalline appearance that reads as white to the eye, and it displays an excellent polish that allows the facets to snap and scintillate under light. Clarity has been assessed as very slightly included at eye level, which for educated buyers signals inclusions that are minimal, do not interrupt the gem’s transparency, and act as a natural fingerprint confirming its origin and authenticity. Importantly, this jeremejevite is untreated, no enhancement, and comes from Namibia, a source noted for producing high quality, collector grade specimens.

From a gemological perspective the combination of a 10.34 carat weight and the precise dimensions of 12.84 x 11.23 x 9.17 mm make this jeremejevite notable for both presence and proportional beauty. The radiant cut, executed with excellent polish, enhances the gem’s optical performance by balancing brilliance and dispersion, and by controlling light leakage within the stone. The very slightly included clarity grade means that, at typical viewing distances, the stone reads as eye clean while still retaining the microscopic characteristics that confirm it is natural. These internal characteristics are valuable to educated buyers because they provide a means of identification and provenance, and they influence both aesthetic and market value. In practical terms jeremejevite has a Mohs hardness around about 6.5 to 7, which places it in a category where it can be worn in jewelry with sensible protections and an appropriate setting design, though it requires more care than harder gemstones such as sapphire or diamond.

The Namibian origin of this jeremejevite adds a layer of desirability and trust for buyers who value traceable provenance. Namibia is known among specialists for producing jeremejevite specimens with good clarity and attractive colorless to pale hues, and an unenhanced stone from this region carries both historical and collector significance. Natural jeremejevite is rare in the marketplace, making high quality examples at this carat weight uncommon and sought after by museums, private collectors, and connoisseurs. The absence of enhancement, full transparency about clarity and cut, and a verified locality from Namibia are the kinds of attributes that informed buyers prioritize when building a curated collection or making an investment in tangible assets. The internal inclusions, described as very slightly included, serve as natural identifiers, and the excellent polish conveys the cutter’s skill in realizing maximum brilliance and beauty from the rough.

When comparing a natural jeremejevite of this quality to lab grown alternatives educated buyers should consider three principal advantages that natural stones provide. First, rarity and collectability are inherent to natural stones, especially to species such as jeremejevite that occur only in limited localities. The finite supply, combined with documented origin from Namibia, supports long term interest and potential appreciation in value, whereas lab grown stones are produced in controlled environments and are more abundant by comparison. Second, natural stones carry geological history and subtle chemical fingerprints that affect color nuances, inclusions, and optical behavior in ways that are unique to each specimen, creating aesthetic and scientific interest that lab grown stones cannot replicate. Third, market perception matters for resale and legacy value, and many collectors and investors continue to place a premium on natural, untreated material, particularly when it is well documented and of high craftsmanship. At The Natural Gemstone Company we emphasize responsible sourcing, full disclosure that this stone has no enhancement, and our readiness to assist with independent gemological reporting for buyers who require certification. If you seek a high profile, rare, and visually remarkable jeremejevite with proven Namibian provenance and transparent gemological attributes, this 10.34 carat radiant shape white jeremejevite represents a compelling option.

title: PR13409
descriptionHtml:
This pair of natural ametrines from Brazil presents precise proportions and deliberate cutting decisions intended to maximize both clarity and the striking bi color effect that defines this species. The stones weigh 3.10 carats and 3.22 carats respectively, and measure 9.26 x 8.23 x 5.56 mm and 9.29 x 8.16 x 5.64 mm. When averaged across length and width these dimensions correspond to depths of approximately 63.6 percent and 64.7 percent, values that sit within the ideal range for step cut gemstones and which preserve broad, even color planes without sacrificing light return. Both stones are fashioned in a traditional emerald cut, employing parallel step facets across the crown and pavilion and a generous table that reinforces linear color zoning rather than dispersing it. Clarity is graded as very very slightly included, evaluated at eye level, which in practice means only minimal internal features are present and none interfere with the primary color transition between purple and golden yellow. The polish is excellent, and no enhancement has been applied, ensuring the observed tones and zoning are intrinsic to the crystal and intact from the mine to the gem.

From a lapidary and craftsmanship perspective these ametrines demonstrate disciplined faceting and symmetry control. The emerald cut was chosen to emphasize planar color separation, so facet junctions on the crown and pavilion are executed with long, even facet lines that produce crisp step reflections rather than scintillation spots. The pavilion depths have been cut to maintain a controlled light path that preserves contrast between the amethyst and citrine zones, while the crown angles are shallow enough to allow the table to act as a viewing window for the internal bicolor effect. Attention to girdle uniformity and alignment is evident when the pair is viewed side by side, which is critical for matching pairs intended for twin mountings. The very very slightly included clarity grade offers the advantage of structural integrity and natural origin verification, while the lack of any thermal or irradiation enhancement maintains predictable wear behavior and long term color stability. Origin from Brazil is noteworthy, as Brazilian ametrines often display distinct, well defined bi color zoning accompanied by saturated medium intensity in both purple and golden tones, a combination that is well respected among collectors and designers alike.

When compared to other matched gemstone pairs the aesthetic of this emerald cut ametrine set is characterized by directional color drama rather than isotropic color saturation. In contrast to matched amethyst pairs these ametrines offer dual tonal versatility, allowing a single piece to read as purple dominant or yellow dominant depending on mounting orientation and ambient light spectrum. Compared to pairs of matched citrines the ametrine pair introduces cool warm interplay, which can lend greater complexity to fine jewelry designs. Against matched bi color tourmalines the ametrine pair tends to present broader, flatter color planes with less windowing and more of a stepped gradient, due to the combined effect of the emerald cut and the inherent color zoning mechanism of ametrine mineralogy. For designers seeking symmetry the pair matches closely in length width and depth percentages, enabling them to be set as mirror images for earrings, cufflinks, or a matched trilogy when supplemented by a third stone. For settings that emphasize the bicolor nature consider an east west orientation to present the color split as a straight horizon, or a diagonal mount to create an internal contrast line that shifts with movement. At The Natural Gemstone Company we consider this pair an exemplar of matched bi color stones, offering technical excellence in cut and finish, natural Brazilian origin, and a visual performance that outperforms uniform single tone pairs when the goal is to evoke contrast, versatility, and refined lapidary execution.

title: PR13703
descriptionHtml:
These two cushion shaped orangish red malaya garnets present a rare combination of balance and beauty, making them an outstanding choice for paired gemstone designs. The pair weighs 0.56 carats and 0.66 carats respectively, and their measured proportions are 5.38 by 3.73 by 2.86 millimeters and 5.79 by 3.90 by 3.08 millimeters. Each stone is fashioned in a mixed brilliant cut to maximize both scintillation and depth of color, and both display a medium color intensity that flatters a wide range of metal settings. Clarity for the pair is graded as very slightly included, evaluated at eye level, and they have an excellent polish that allows light to pass and reflect in a consistently pleasing manner. These Malaya garnets originate from Tanzania and have been heat treated, a standard enhancement that stabilizes and enhances their attractive orangish red tones while preserving their natural charm. The Natural Gemstone Company is proud to present this matched pair as a refined option for designers and collectors who demand both visual harmony and gemological integrity.

What sets this pair apart in practical design terms is their matching clarity, an attribute that is often overlooked but crucial when creating symmetrical jewelry. When two stones are set side by side in earrings, a pendant with twin stones, or in a three stone ring as companion accents, matching clarity ensures that both stones transmit light in the same way, avoiding the distracting imbalance that can occur when one stone appears cloudier or more included to the naked eye. With both of these garnets evaluated as very slightly included at eye level, you receive the effect of near eye clean appearance without the premium price of completely inclusion free material. The similar cut style and excellent polish further reinforce symmetry, because faceting alignment and surface finish control reflections and highlights. In short, these garnets behave as a matched optical unit, returning light evenly and producing a pleasing, symmetrical sparkle that greatly simplifies design decisions and reduces the need for compensatory mounting techniques.

Compared to other matched pairs on the market, this duo offers advantages in several key areas, quality, value, and uniqueness. Many commercially available pairs will be matched primarily by carat weight or color, while allowing divergence in clarity or polish that becomes obvious once set. This Tanzanian pair from The Natural Gemstone Company exhibits a more holistic match, with congruent clarity and finish that make them perform together rather than as two disparate stones. In terms of value, heat treatment is an accepted and reversible enhancement that improves color stability and saturation, and because these stones are medium intensity, they show lively color without appearing overworked. The mixed brilliant cut delivers a balance of table brightness and pavilion fire, which often outperforms single facet styles in small to medium sized stones. Uniqueness comes from the malaya garnet itself, a distinct and increasingly sought after variety that offers a warm interplay of pink, orange, and red that is difficult to replicate in more common gems. When you compare these garnets to other options such as matched sapphires, tourmalines, or spinels, their color personality and matched optical behavior give them a distinctive presence that elevates both classic and contemporary designs.

For jewelers and private clients who want a matched pair that simplifies design choices while delivering professional results, these malaya garnets are an excellent pick. Their cushion shape lends itself to both vintage inspired and modern settings, and their slight difference in weight is visually compensated by their closely matched proportions and matching clarity. Settings that emphasize symmetry will benefit directly from the pair, because the matched clarity and excellent polish reduce the need for heavy bezels or obscuring mounts, allowing the gems themselves to be the focal point. From a practical standpoint, the dimensions and mixed brilliant faceting make them suitable for bezel set, prong set, or halo treatments, and their medium color intensity pairs well with warm and neutral metals. At The Natural Gemstone Company we focus on sourcing stones that perform in real world settings, and this pair exemplifies that philosophy by offering consistent light return, matched appearance, and a balanced value proposition. If you are planning a set of earrings, a matched pendant pair, or twin accents in a custom piece, these Malaya garnets will give you a predictable and beautiful result, and we are available to advise on mounting options and design considerations to ensure the final piece fully benefits from their matched clarity and exceptional polish.

There has been no enhancement, the origin is Ceylon, Sri Lanka, and the gem is offered by The Natural Gemstone Company with full disclosure of its natural state and provenance.

The greenish yellow hue of this sinhalite occupies a rare position between olive green and vivid chartreuse, a balance that responds strikingly to both warm and cool metal tones. In direct lighting the stone displays a focused, lively inner glow, while in softer ambient light it presents a more subdued, elegant tone, creating visual versatility for different jewelry applications. The mixed brilliant cut contributes to a crisp interplay of light and dark facets, increasing contrast that sharpens the perceived color and gives faceted surfaces a jewel like depth. When set in a bezel or a minimal prong setting the color becomes a focal point, and when paired with accent stones the sinhalite holds its own without being overwhelmed, making it adaptable to designs that range from classic solitaires to contemporary multi stone arrangements.

From a design perspective this 2.05 carat oval sinhalite is suitable for a range of jewelry types, including rings, pendants, and drop earrings, where the elongated oval silhouette provides a flattering visual line. In pendant and earring settings the gem's medium color intensity will remain striking at a distance, and the optic balance between sparkle and color makes it an excellent candidate for halo treatments using small white diamonds to increase perceived size and contrast. Care for this natural sinhalite consists of routine gentle cleaning with warm soapy water and a soft brush, avoiding harsh ultrasonic treatments and sudden thermal shocks, to preserve the cutting polish and the integrity of the gem over time.

The Natural Gemstone Company provides this sinhalite with transparent documentation of its attributes, including carat weight, exact measurements, cut style, clarity assessment, color intensity, polish grade, absence of enhancement, and geographic origin. The provenance from Ceylon, Sri Lanka, underscores the gem's geological pedigree and aligns with our commitment to sourcing naturally occurring material from respected origins. For custom design projects our gem specialists can advise on metal choices, prong counts, and setting styles to ensure the gem's greenish yellow vibrancy remains the central visual element, while accommodating practical considerations for wearability and security. This sinhalite exemplifies a refined balance between natural color, optical performance, and practical proportions, qualities that allow it to stand out confidently in any jewelry setting and to retain its presence as a distinctive focal point for years to come.

Technical considerations for use and care are important given the dye treatment and microcrystalline silica structure. Dye treated agate will retain stable color under normal wearing conditions, however prolonged exposure to strong solvents, ultrasonic cleaners, or prolonged heat can affect dye stability, therefore mechanical setting methods and mild cleaning are recommended. The cabochon cut here minimizes internal stress and masks minor internal fractures, while the excellent polish enhances band contrast and reduces the need for aggressive lighting to reveal pattern. For designers, recommended settings include low profile bezels for pendants to preserve the pear outline, and three prong tips with custom back plates for earrings to accommodate the thinner pavilion of one stone, ensuring secure mounting without overdrilling. Opal type, White Opal. White Opal generally presents a pale body tone with potential for play of color on suitable specimens, but is noted here solely as a reference opal type and is not a component of this dyed agate pair.

Measuring 17.82 x 12.29 x 7.03 mm, this translucent pear cabochon presents a balanced presence that is both wearable and striking. The cabochon cut is not merely an aesthetic choice, it is the key to how this lemon rutilated quartz reveals its inner life. Unlike faceted gems that rely on planes and angles to fracture and return light, a polished cabochon crown draws light across a smooth dome, allowing translucency and internal structures to become the primary performers. In this quartz the golden rutile needles are the signature feature, and the cabochon form amplifies the way light travels through the crystal, scattering gently off each needle and through the stone to produce depth and a living glow. With medium color intensity the lemon tone bathes the rutile in warmth, and the excellent polish on the dome creates a clean reflective skin that enhances surface lustre without obscuring the internal play. Where rutile needles align they can create a silky sheen or a subtle chatoyant effect, and when they fan or cross they form shimmering lattices that shift with every turn of the wrist. Because the gem is eye clean in the traditional sense, the rutiles are seen as golden inclusions that add character rather than flaws, and the cabochon cut allows those inclusions to breathe and perform, catching light from different angles and deepening the sense of three dimensionality within the stone.

For someone who needs a piece that solves both stylistic and emotional needs, this lemon rutilated quartz is the answer. It offers a unique compromise between sparkle and serenity, a gem that will feel intimate in a bezel setting where the cabochon is protected and its glow is contained, or radiant in a prong or halo mounting that lets light travel through the dome and accentuates the pear shape. Collectors will appreciate the provenance from Ceylon Sri Lanka and the natural, untreated state of the stone, while a couple seeking an engagement gem will find in this cabochon a conversation starter that is elegant, durable, and unmistakably personal. The Natural Gemstone Company stands behind this example for its quality and beauty, and we can advise on settings, mounting options, and care that preserve the polish and translucency for generations. This rutilated quartz is more than a mineral, it is a resolved search, a piece that replaces uncertainty with confidence, and it is ready to be the centerpiece that completes your collection or seals a promise.

descriptionHtml:
This matched pair of rutilated quartz cabochons offered by The Natural Gemstone Company presents clear, educational detail for a discerning buyer. The stones weigh 3.46 carats and 3.60 carats respectively, with precise dimensions of 9.09 x 9.06 x 5.35 mm and 9.26 x 9.13 x 5.28 mm, and are fashioned into round cabochon shapes that emphasize internal character rather than faceted brilliance. The body color is a warm brown with medium color intensity, and the stones show fine golden to amber rutile needle inclusions that create a distinctive silky shimmer and attractive internal patterning. Clarity is graded slightly included when evaluated at eye level, which is typical and desirable for rutilated quartz because the rutile needles are the primary aesthetic feature. The polish is excellent, surfaces are smooth and reflective, and there is no enhancement applied to these natural gems. The material is sourced from Ceylon Sri Lanka, a locality known for producing rutilated quartz with clean color and well developed rutile networks. For collectors who are also interested in complementary materials, we also note the opal type White Opal as part of related offerings within our inventory.

From a practical perspective these rutilated quartz cabochons are well suited to daily wear because quartz ranks at seven on the Mohs hardness scale, providing a solid balance of scratch resistance and workability for jewelers. The cabochon cut reduces vulnerability to edge chipping because there are no sharp facets, and the internal rutile needles do not generally compromise toughness, although care should be taken to avoid hard knocks that could cause fracture in any crystalline gem. Because these stones are natural and not enhanced, they retain their long term stability under ordinary conditions. Recommended care is routine cleaning with warm soapy water and a soft brush, avoiding prolonged exposure to harsh chemicals, acids, or steam cleaning. For settings, secure bezel or well designed prong settings are advised for rings and earrings to protect the girdle and provide daily security. The combination of matched size, weight, origin, and excellent polish makes this pair an excellent choice for a thoughtful custom set or classic stud earrings, and it represents transparent, factual value for an educated buyer seeking quality natural gems from The Natural Gemstone Company.

title: K15975
descriptionHtml:
This luminous marquise shaped smoky quartz weighs 5.97 carats, measuring 16.91 x 9.28 x 5.01 mm, a refined size that balances presence with versatility. Cut as a smooth cabochon, this stone presents a gently domed profile that enhances its deep, brown tones without faceting, showcasing an intense color that reads rich and velvety from every angle. Transparency is excellent for a cabochon of this character, and clarity is evaluated as very very slightly included at eye level, meaning the stone appears clean and pure to the immediate observer, with only the most careful scrutiny revealing minute natural markings. The polish on this gem is excellent, resulting in a glasslike surface that captures and reflects light with a soft, luminous sheen, while the lack of any enhancement confirms the stone is wholly natural and stable. Originating from Brazil, this smoky quartz carries the geological authenticity and provenance that collectors and designers prize, making it a reliable and honorable choice for both heirloom pieces and contemporary creations.

The history of smoky quartz is rich and resonant, intertwined with traditions that span continents and centuries, a gem that has long served as a talisman and a symbol of earthbound elegance. In ancient times this variety of quartz was revered for its grounding qualities and was often fashioned into protective amulets and signet ornaments, carrying with it a sense of rooted longevity. During the Victorian era smoky quartz found favor in mourning jewelry and in pieces that favored depth of tone and introspective beauty, prized for its warm, sympathetic hues that suggested both dignity and solace. The marquise silhouette itself is steeped in classical heritage, a shape that first captured popular imagination in European courts, offering an elongated, heraldic profile that flatters the hand and elongates a setting, while the cabochon cut recalls antiquity and the artisanal traditions of early gemcutters who polished stones by hand to reveal their inner glow. Together, the marquise form and the cabochon finish create a timeless language of design, one that speaks to buyers who value continuity, craftsmanship, and a connection to the past.

At The Natural Gemstone Company we present this marquise cabochon smoky quartz as a piece ready to be set into a range of jewelry styles, from a stately cocktail ring that emphasizes the stone's length, to a pendant that allows the gem to rest against the heart, to a bespoke pair of earrings where matched stones could mirror one another. The gentle dome of the cabochon lends itself beautifully to bezel settings or to secure prong styles that showcase the stone without obscuring its silhouette, and the intense brown coloration pairs especially well with warm metals such as yellow gold and rose gold, while contrasting elegantly with cool tones like sterling silver or platinum. For designers and collectors who prefer an antique or heritage aesthetic, this smoky quartz adapts readily to period inspired settings, and for those pursuing a modern minimalist direction, the stone offers a singular, understated statement. We encourage close consideration of the 16.91 x 9.28 x 5.01 mm dimensions when planning your setting, as these proportions make the gem adaptable to both vertical and horizontal orientations. As with all of our gemstones, this smoky quartz comes with the assurance of natural origin, fine craftsmanship in cutting and polishing, and the attentive service of our team at The Natural Gemstone Company, ready to provide additional images, mounting suggestions, or custom design consultations to ensure the finished piece honors both the material and the history it carries.

From a design application perspective, these stones are specifically well suited to statement earring formats used in high fashion contexts, where scale, surface interest, and refined color are essential. The medium color intensity and warm brown hue pair effectively with yellow gold for a tonal, elevated aesthetic, and conversely with white gold or platinum when a cooler, contrasted look is desired. The checkerboard facet pattern softens direct sparkle and instead emphasizes flashes and depth, making the stones suitable for larger scale dangles, clustered settings, and sculptural metal frameworks where light interplay is a design feature. Their dimensions permit confident use in stud formats that read as substantial without overwhelming the ear, and they also accommodate halo and multi stone surrounds that amplify presence while maintaining a measured refinement.

All product attributes have been assessed and recorded by The Natural Gemstone Company quality team to provide a clear specification for designers and jewelers. The stones are identified as round brown smoky quartz, 2.23 carats and 2.35 carats, dimensions as stated, checkerboard cut, clarity graded eye clean at eye level, medium color intensity, excellent polish, heat treated enhancement, origin Brazil. For practical handling, standard care for quartz is recommended, avoiding hard knocks and prolonged exposure to strong chemicals, and routine cleaning with mild soapy water and a soft brush will preserve surface luster. The documented specifications support accurate design planning, and the measured consistency and finish of the pair make them a reliable option for high fashion statement earrings that require both aesthetic impact and technical predictability.

title: K25245
descriptionHtml:
This specimen is a transparent 6.88 carat radiant shaped andesine, measuring 12.77 x 11.23 x 7.93 mm, exhibiting a warm orangish brown body tone and intense color saturation. The cutting style is faceted with a modern radiant pavilion and crown configuration that blends step and brilliant faceting to optimize both color and light return, and the polish grade is excellent. Clarity is graded as very slightly included when evaluated at eye level, which in practice yields high visual transparency and minimal impact on light transmission. The material has been heat treated to enhance and stabilize the orange brown hue, and the documented origin is Africa, which in this case corresponds to material within the plagioclase feldspar series that presents consistent crystal structure and color response to controlled thermal enhancement. The Natural Gemstone Company provides this piece as a calibrated, precisely executed radiant cut that balances carat weight, face up size, and optical performance.

From a cutting and faceting perspective the radiant cut on this andesine is engineered to capitalize on the gemological properties of plagioclase feldspar. Radiant cuts typically employ a crown arrangement of small star and kite facets combined with a pavilion of mixed brilliant and modified step facets, and that approach is evident here in the distribution of light return and the pattern of scintillation across the table. The facet junctions are tight and the polish is carried to an excellent finish, both of which minimize surface scattering and allow the inherent vitreous luster of andesine to predominate. Andesine has a refractive index in the neighborhood of 1.56 to 1.58, and a relatively low birefringence, which means that the stone produces broad, even flashes of light rather than the high contrast pinfire scintillation seen in higher refractive index gems. The result in this radiant cut is a lively but tempered brilliance, with the intense orangish brown color remaining the dominant visual attribute, and with sparkle that is most apparent under focused light sources.

When compared to other gemstones in the plagioclase family and to commonly encountered transparent gems used in the same jewelries, the reflective qualities of this andesine are distinctive. Against labradorite, which exhibits strong labradorescence and schiller as an interference phenomenon, this andesine is straightforwardly transparent and color driven, without the directional sheen that can mask body color. Against sunstone, which shows aventurescence from oriented platelets and can display metallic glitter, the andesine presents a cleaner, more evenly saturated surface that emphasizes hue and tone over metallic sparkle. Compared to higher refractive index stones such as sapphire and spinel, andesine will exhibit less intense brilliance and lower dispersion, therefore it does not produce the same amount of white light return or spectral fire, but it compensates with a deeper, more enveloping color presence and broad flash patterns that are less fragmented. Relative to topaz and tourmaline, with refractive indices that are somewhat higher, this andesine provides a softer but more uniform reflective character, and the radiant cut here enhances perceived brightness by increasing the number of small facets that catch light without introducing excessive contrast. The overall visual effect is a balance between color dominance and controlled optical activity, making the piece suitable for designs where color depth and warm tone are the primary aesthetic goals.

From the standpoint of craftsmanship and practical wearability the cut proportions and corner faceting of the radiant shape provide an efficient use of rough that yields a generous face up appearance at 6.88 carats, while offering mechanical durability through trimmed corners that reduce chipping risk. The excellent polish and tight facet symmetry indicate careful lapidary control during the cutting process, and the heat treatment applied is a standard and stable enhancement for andesine that improves color uniformity without compromising durability. For jewelry settings the stone performs well in rings, pendants, and earrings where its intense color can be displayed against complementary metal tones, and the medium to strong light return means it will remain visible and eye catching under indoor lighting as well as natural daylight. The Natural Gemstone Company stands behind the documented properties of this andesine and can provide additional technical data, imaging, and certification on request, and professional buyers are invited to evaluate the piece in person to assess the interplay of facet architecture, body color, and sparkle that this precisely cut radiant andesine delivers.

title: K25246
descriptionHtml:
A rare and arresting treasure, this transparent 3.65 carat oval andesine presents an orangish brown heart that seems to glow from within, a color so warm and assured it commands attention the moment it catches the light. Measuring 12.15 by 9.88 by 6.12 millimeters, the gem is proportioned for both presence and versatility, an ideal size to anchor a ring for the hand that seeks distinction, or to become the centerpiece of a pendant that speaks of quiet confidence. The cutting style is faceted, executed as a mixed brilliant cut to balance scintillation and depth, and the surface carries an excellent polish that allows each facet to sing. Clarity is graded slightly included evaluated at eye level, a natural signature that whispers of authenticity rather than perfection, and the color intensity is intense, a deep and resonant tone that is both sophisticated and sensuous. Enhancement by heat treatment has been applied to elevate and stabilize the hue, a considered and common intervention that reveals the stone at its most flattering, while its origin in Africa lends a provenance both storied and noble. At The Natural Gemstone Company we curate such stones not merely as ornaments, but as heirloom intentions, each offering a narrative that is as compelling as the light it returns.

To conceive how such a stone came to be is to imagine processes that unfolded over geological epochs, an exquisite choreography of heat, pressure, and elemental alchemy. Deep within the continental crust of ancient Africa, when mountains were young and the subterranean world was a realm of incandescent motion, pockets of molten rock cooled in isolation. Within those crucibles, molecules arranged themselves into ordered lattices, and plagioclase feldspar began to crystallize. Our andesine is a member of that plagioclase family, and its warm orangish brown derives from the subtle interplay of trace elements and structural vacancies within the crystal lattice. Over millions of years, as temperatures eased and chemical gradients shifted, tiny amounts of copper and iron migrated into the growing crystal, imparting hues that ranged from soft honey to a more saturated russet when captured and concentrated in just the right way. Slow cooling allowed clarity to develop, a transparency that would later allow light to travel through the gem and reflect back in flashes of brilliance. Minute inclusions were trapped during this patient formation, microscopic signatures that record the conditions of the earth long before human hands learned to recognize and revere such forms.

The passage from subterranean genesis to polished jewel is itself a saga of upheaval and refinement. Tectonic forces folded and uplifted the host rocks, exposing once hidden veins to the elements, while cycles of weathering and riverine transport liberated crystals from their ancient matrices and carried them toward surface deposits. Time and erosion polished some roughs into rounded pebbles, while others waited until a miner descended into a new seam and cupped a raw crystal in a callused palm. Selected specimens, those that exhibited exceptional color and clarity, were entrusted to cutters who approach each rough with both technical mastery and aesthetic sensibility. This andesine was shaped into an elegant oval, the mixed brilliant cut chosen to maximize both sparkle and color saturation, while maintaining generous depth for a jewel that reads with presence on the skin. Heat treatment was applied with precision, a careful thermal conversation that coaxed the most desirable tone from the stone without compromising its structural integrity. The excellent polish gives each facet a mirror finish, so that when you move, light plays across the surface like a private constellation. The slightly included clarity grade is not a flaw, it is provenance visible, an intimate map of the stone’s journey that assures the wearer of authenticity and natural origin.

To possess this andesine is to claim a small fragment of deep time, refined into an object of intention that elevates every gesture. It is a stone for those who appreciate subtle power rather than ostentation, for collectors who value narrative as much as beauty, and for connoisseurs whose taste is defined by discernment. Imagine this gem set in warm gold to echo its internal radiance, or in cool platinum to provide a modern contrast that makes the orangish brown appear even richer. In a ring it becomes a signature of authority, in a necklace it becomes the quiet center of an evening where impressions are formed and remembered. At The Natural Gemstone Company we stand behind the careful provenance and the expert craftsmanship that bring such stones to market, and we understand that the purchase of a gemstone is often the beginning of a story to be told across generations. This andesine, with its measured weight, thoughtful proportions, and intense color, is more than a jewel, it is a declaration of refined taste, an emblem of achievement, and a companion to the moments when one chooses to be seen as someone who values the rare and the real.

title: K12629
descriptionHtml:
This 10.74 carat oval golden brown tiger eye from South Africa, offered by The Natural Gemstone Company, is presented as an opaque cabochon with dimensions of 18.09 x 13.09 x 6.60 mm. The piece is a traditional domed cabochon, oval outline, with a well centered apex and symmetrical profile that follows classical cabochon geometry. The weight to size ratio is consistent with dense chatoyant quartz material, and the measurement data indicate a substantial depth of 6.60 mm that preserves the internal fiber parallelism responsible for the tiger eye effect. The polish on the dome is graded excellent, producing broad specular reflections across the surface, and no enhancements have been applied to the material, preserving its natural appearance and structural integrity.

The cutting style is a high domed cabochon cut executed to emphasize the chatoyant band, with the fiber alignment oriented parallel to the long axis of the oval to produce a single, strong eye when viewed under directional light. The dome height has been selected to balance mass and optical performance, creating a pleasing dome curvature that produces a crisp band without excessive windowing at the sides. Symmetry of the outline is controlled to within tight tolerances so that the band remains centered as the stone is rotated. The surface exhibits an excellent polish, free from polishing lines and with only minimal lap residue under high magnification, indicating that the final lapping stages were carefully executed. Edge finishing flows smoothly into the base, and the stone sits flat on a plane surface when inspected, confirming a properly leveled pavilion or base for secure setting.

Optically the material displays the hallmark silky chatoyancy of tiger eye, with a warm golden brown main body color and a distinct reflective band that shifts with the angle of incident light. Although the color intensity field is recorded as n a in the dataset, visual assessment places the tone in the medium to medium dark range with moderate saturation, producing a classic golden brown appearance. The band itself exhibits higher reflectivity and appears slightly warmer in hue than the surrounding body color, creating a measurable contrast that enhances the perceived depth. Internal structure includes the parallel fibrous inclusions typical of pseudomorphous quartz after amphibole, oriented to produce a single linear eye. No fractures or cleavage planes are evident that would compromise toughness, and no dye or resin treatments were detected, confirming the untreated status of the piece.

From a lapidary and setting perspective, the dimensions and dome profile recommend specific mounting strategies to maximize optical effect and mechanical security. For jewelry applications that prioritize chatoyancy, orient the long axis of the oval parallel to the expected viewing orientation so the eye runs across the face of the piece. A low to medium height bezel setting will protect the dome and maintain optical performance, while allowing sufficient light to sweep the band. For rings that will receive frequent impact, a recessed bezel combined with a strong seat at the base will reduce risk of edge chipping. The 6.60 mm thickness provides good material mass for deep settings, and the stone can be securely held with conventional bezel or prong systems designed for cabochon shapes, noting that the smooth base provides reliable adhesion surface if additional securing is required in mixed metal designs.

As a sourced and authenticated specimen from South Africa, this tiger eye exemplifies natural formation and careful cutting, and it is offered by The Natural Gemstone Company with full disclosure of weight, dimensions, cut style, polish grade, enhancement status, and origin. Care recommendations include routine cleaning with warm water and mild detergent, avoiding ultrasonic cleaners and harsh chemicals that could affect surface polish over time. When storing, protect the dome from hard contact with other stones to preserve the excellent polish. For commissioning custom settings or requesting additional imagery or viewing under directional light to assess the chatoyancy, contact The Natural Gemstone Company for further technical data and handling guidance, and for shipping and certification options.

This listing from The Natural Gemstone Company presents one beautiful opaque green malachite, round shape, 14.58 carat, with precise dimensions of 13.11 x 13.13 x 8.23 mm. The stone has been cut en cabochon to best display malachite characteristic banding, and it exhibits an excellent polish that gives a rich satiny luster across the dome. As an opaque material, malachite is evaluated differently than transparent gems, and the key visual criteria are color saturation, pattern definition, and surface finish. This particular example shows deep, vivid green tones with well defined concentric banding and botryoidal patterns that are highly desirable to collectors and designers who prize natural texture and contrast. The cabochon form and the nearly symmetrical round outline make this piece especially suitable for a variety of settings, including classic bezels and sculptural mounts that emphasize the stone as a focal element.

From a gemological perspective, malachite is a copper carbonate hydroxide mineral, and Russian malachite, especially material from the Ural region, carries historical and provenance value that sophisticated buyers recognize. The origin being Russia means the specimen likely derives from deposits that produced some of the most iconic and collectible malachite in the 19th and early 20th centuries, which can add a premium compared with anonymous sources. Clarity grading for malachite centers on internal pattern clarity and absence of unwanted inclusions or fractures that interrupt the banding. This stone is opaque by nature, and the banding patterns are continuous and sharp, indicating a high quality rough and careful cutting. The listing notes no enhancement, which is important because treatments such as stabilization or dyeing are sometimes applied to lower grade material. The absence of enhancement confirms that what you see is the natural color and pattern, preserved by skilled lapidary work. The excellent polish further elevates the apparent depth and contrast of the bands, and it reduces the need for additional finishing after setting.

When assessing value for use in jewelry or as a collector specimen, several practical and aesthetic factors make this malachite noteworthy. The weight of 14.58 carat combined with a substantial dome height of 8.23 mm provides a strong visual presence in a ring, pendant, or as part of a multi stone composition. The round cabochon shape is universally compatible with many design languages, and the symmetry of 13.11 x 13.13 mm suggests accurate cutting that will sit evenly in a bezel or frame. Buyers should also consider physical characteristics, malachite is relatively soft on the Mohs scale, and it requires protective settings and mindful wear, so bezel or closed mountings are recommended to prevent abrasion. Care instructions are straightforward, use a soft cloth for cleaning, avoid ultrasonic cleaners and chemical solvents, and remove jewelry for activities that could expose the stone to impact or harsh chemicals. For collectors, the Russian origin and untreated status are primary value drivers, and for designers, the combination of vivid banding, size, and polish present a ready to set focal gem that will photograph and display exceptionally.

title: PR12660
descriptionHtml:
This pair of Russian malachites offered by The Natural Gemstone Company consists of two substantial oval cabochons weighing 25.37 carats and 27.14 carats respectively, presenting a rich bluish green hue across an opaque body. The material exhibits classic malachite banding with well defined concentric and linear growth lines that provide depth and visual texture at multiple viewing angles. Because these stones are opaque, traditional color intensity grading is not applicable, therefore assessment focuses on hue uniformity, band contrast, and translucency or lack thereof. Both stones display a cool green leaning toward blue in the midtones, with slightly darker concentric banding that enhances perceived richness and gives the cabochons a visually layered appearance. Origin is Russia, which is known for producing malachite with exceptionally clear band separations and saturated tones, and these specimens conform to that expectation while remaining entirely natural and untreated.

Measured dimensions are 16.14 x 14.08 x 10.86 mm for the 25.37 carat piece, and 16.06 x 13.94 x 11.16 mm for the 27.14 carat piece, with both exhibiting an oval outline and a domed cabochon profile. The cutting approach prioritizes symmetry and a balanced dome height to maximize the banding rhythm across the face of each stone, which is essential for matched pairs intended for earrings or matched set elements. The domes show a consistent curvature from center to girdle, which preserves optical continuity between the pair and minimizes visual discontinuity when set side by side. Edge transitions are clean and uniform, facilitating secure bezel seating without the need for extensive metal modification. The excellent polish achieved on both surfaces results in a high gloss finish that accentuates the band contrast and gives specular highlights, while also revealing the internal fibrous layering without any waxy or dull areas.

From a craftsmanship perspective, these cabochons reflect careful attention to orientation and band alignment during preforming and final shaping. Malachite is microcrystalline and commonly exhibits foliation and cleavage planes that require controlled removal strategies to avoid lamellar separation, and the lapidary work here demonstrates conservative material removal to preserve structural integrity. The matching process prioritized weight balance, face dimensions, and band continuity, resulting in two pieces that are closely calibrated for paired use, notwithstanding minor natural variation in band geometry that contributes to their distinct character. No heat treatment, dyeing, impregnation, or stabilization has been applied, preserving original surface chemistry and porosity characteristics, and the no enhancement status simplifies both valuation and long term care considerations.

For jewelry integration and longer term preservation, these malachite cabochons are well suited to bezel and flush settings that protect exposed edges and reduce the risk of impact or abrasion, given malachite hardness and its susceptibility to acid and household chemicals. Recommended mounting practices include low profile bezels with a slight lip to shelter the girdle, and the use of inert setting materials to avoid chemical interaction. Cleaning should be accomplished with a soft dry cloth or a slightly damp cloth using distilled water only, avoiding ultrasonic or steam cleaning, and avoiding contact with acids or bleaching agents. The natural banding and color saturation make these stones ideal for classic matched earring pairs, complementary center stones in matched pendant and ring combinations, or as focal elements in bespoke designs where symmetry and paired rhythm are important. The Natural Gemstone Company stands behind the origin and untreated nature of these Russian malachites, and we can provide additional photographic detail or loupe level imagery upon request to assist in final design and appraisal decisions.

Right away these stones stand apart from many market listings that offer smaller, thinner, or heavily treated material. Where commercial lots often include stabilized or dyed pieces to achieve uniform hue, this pair remains chemically untouched, preserving natural texture and inherent banding. The cabochon form emphasizes gentle peach tones and creamy band patterns rather than relying on added color or fillers. Customers who compare listings will notice that similar carat weights elsewhere are commonly single pieces or mismatched pairs, whereas this set arrives balanced and ready for matched settings. The combination of size and symmetry gives a visual weight that makes the gems feel present in a design, yet the medium intensity keeps them wearable for daily jewelry without overwhelming other elements.

When comparing these peach rhodochrosites to other rhodochrosite offerings on the market, especially the vivid pink Argentine material, buyers should understand the distinction and value proposition. Argentine rhodochrosite tends to favor saturated rose tones and sometimes translucency, often commanding high prices for collector grade pieces. These Australian peach rhodochrosites offer a different aesthetic, a subtle and elegant warmth with charming banding that plays well against both warm and cool metals. Unlike imported reconstituted slabs that are commonly sliced to yield many thin cabochons, these stones are substantial in depth which preserves integrity and reduces the risk of breakage during setting. The excellent polish elevates the surface luster so that light skims beautifully across the domes, creating a soft glow that is difficult to replicate in mass market or low quality cuts. For designers and private collectors who want a refined, natural look in matched earrings or cufflinks, this pair outperforms many lower grade or treated alternatives.

Value is a decisive factor for many buyers so it is worth contrasting this natural, untreated pair with treated or composite stones that appear similar at first glance but lack long term appeal. Treated rhodochrosites, whether stabilized with resin or dyed, can lose color or exhibit surface crazing over time and under heat. Reconstituted material often has visible seams or repetitive patterning once examined closely. These Australian cabochons show continuous natural banding that reads as unique on each stone while still presenting a harmonious match. The absence of enhancements means buyers receive provenance and authenticity that increase resale value and collector interest. Paired with White Opal accents, which are noted here as White Opal, the peach rhodochrosites create a sophisticated contrast, the opal providing iridescent flashes while the rhodochrosite supplies a gentle, earthy warmth. This pairing is superior to combinations that rely on synthetic opals or low grade fillers, because the color play and natural textures are real and enduring. The Natural Gemstone Company can advise on mounting approaches that protect the stones while showcasing their matched nature, such as bezel settings that support the cabochon sides or low prong designs that highlight the domed surfaces.

We stand behind the sourcing and the description, and The Natural Gemstone Company offers this pair with clear specifications so you can compare accurately with other offerings. The recorded weights, 10.33 carats and 9.40 carats, and the dimensions 14.41 x 14.39 x 5.29 mm and 14.18 x 14.21 x 4.86 mm make it easy to plan settings and visualize scale. The natural, untreated status and Australian origin are important differentiators in a market where treatments are commonplace. For jewelry applications these cabochons are ideal for matched earrings, a pendant set with complementary White Opal highlights, or bespoke pieces that require a sympathetic, understated color palette. Care is straightforward, clean with mild soap and water and avoid prolonged exposure to acids and strong heat that affect many manganese bearing minerals. If you are weighing this pair against other options, consider the combination of size, natural banding, matching quality, and superb polish that makes these rhodochrosites from The Natural Gemstone Company a superior, long lasting choice for both designers and collectors.

The cutter embraced a classic cabochon style, allowing the asterism to become the central story, and an excellent polish finished the surface so the star moves across the dome like a living constellation.

The transformation from rough Madagascar stone to a finished cabochon is a patient, tactile conversation between cutter and crystal. The cabochon cutting style is deliberate, the oval profile chosen to both center the star and fit pleasantly in an array of jewelry settings. As the artisan shaped and polished the stone, light became a collaborator, coaxing a sharp star to appear and glide across the surface when the gem is turned. The dark, opaque bodycolor provides a dramatic stage for that star to take center stage. Because the piece is untreated, its natural textures and internal architecture remain intact, creating a focal point that feels honest and elemental. The result is an object that carries the scent of its origin, the care of human hands, and a quiet intensity that invites close, lingering attention.

When you imagine this 11.11 x 9.23 x 5.02 mm oval cabochon set into jewelry, possibilities unfold like a jeweler’s sketchbook. In a ring, a low bezel setting will protect the gem while offering a modern, architectural silhouette, ideal for an everyday piece that can withstand wear. A four or six prong solitaire mount will lift the cabochon to catch light and emphasize the star, making it the centerpiece of a cocktail ring or an elegant signet alternative. For additional brilliance, consider a halo of small white diamonds or white sapphires to frame the dark stone and amplify visual contrast. As a pendant, the gem sits comfortably within both minimalist bezel frames and ornate vintage inspired mounts, where hand engraving or filigree can echo the stone’s origin story. For a bold masculine expression, think cufflinks or a substantial men’s ring in brushed yellow gold, where the dark star provides a dramatic counterpoint to warm metal. Earrings work beautifully as matched pairs, or as single statement studs paired with diamond accents. Mixed metal settings and asymmetrical designs bring a contemporary edge, while cluster settings can transform the stone into an heirloom style piece. Because the cabochon cut presents a smooth dome, creative options like tension settings or partial bezels give you a balance of security and display, and the gem’s 4.58 carat weight makes it substantial without overpowering.

At The Natural Gemstone Company we celebrate the story each stone carries and offer a full range of customization services to realize that narrative. Our design team can produce sketches and digital mockups, suggest metal choices that enhance the black star, and recommend side stones that complement rather than compete. For protection and everyday wear, we guide clients toward settings that shield the cabochon’s dome while showcasing the star, and we provide care recommendations to keep the gem radiant, recommending gentle cleaning with mild soap and water and avoiding harsh chemicals and extreme heat. Because this gem is natural and untreated, we are happy to provide detailed information about its origin and characteristics on request. Whether you imagine a sleek modern ring that lets the star fly free, a pendant that carries Madagascar’s landscape close to your heart, or an ornate vintage piece that feels like it has a history to tell, this black star diopside is ready to be shaped into something personal.
