title: 2.98 Ct. Red Rubellite Tourmaline Ring 18K Yellow & White J11890
availability: This item is available to ship now
descriptionHtml:
This ring presents a study in contrast and technique, rendered in 18K yellow gold and 18K white gold, with a substantial cushion shaped ruby as the focal point. The yellow gold shank is hand engraved with a repeating foliate motif, executed using traditional gravure tools to produce consistent depth and crisp line work, then finished to a warm high polish that accentuates the metal tone. The upper mounting is executed in 18K white gold, rhodium plated for optimal whiteness, and shaped into a sculptural halo and crown that frame the central ruby while reflecting maximum light into the stone. The transition between yellow and white gold is managed with precision solder joints and seamless finishing, ensuring the visual dichotomy reads as intentional design rather than assembly. Every metal junction is inspected for continuity, and the interior of the band is hallmarked and hand finished to ensure wearer comfort, while the external surfaces receive a combination of high polish and selective satin finishing to enhance contrast between engraved areas and smooth planes.

The central ruby exhibits the optical and material properties consistent with high quality corundum, the crystal system that defines ruby, with a refractive index in the range associated with natural rubies, and a hardness of nine on the Mohs scale that contributes to durable wear. The stone is cut to a cushion outline with a mixed facet scheme, combining brilliant facets on the crown and modified step facets on the pavilion, a configuration that balances fire and color retention. The table is proportioned to preserve saturation, while the crown height and pavilion depth are calibrated to promote internal reflection without inducing a windowing effect. Color is described as a vivid, well saturated red with slight modulation toward the pure red zone under daylight, strong in tone, and responsive to directional light due to modest pleochroism typical of chromium bearing corundum. Clarity character is in keeping with natural ruby, showing internal silk and pinpoint inclusions that act to diffuse light and deepen perceived color, while the cutter minimized surface reaching fractures through careful facet placement and polishing.

The mounting strategy is engineered to both secure and showcase the gemstone, the ruby being held within a sculpted crown of white gold prongs that rise from a pavé halo, creating a continuous luminous collar. The halo comprises bead set round brilliant diamonds, each selected for consistent cut and color grade to provide a uniform scintillation field, and each bead set location is milgrain finished by hand to define edges and prevent light leakage. The gallery is open and pierced to allow maximum light entry from the pavilion and to facilitate cleaning, the interior contours polished to a satin finish that reduces glare. The shank tapers subtly toward the base to maintain balance and comfort, while the hand engraving extends from shoulder to midpoint to create a visual bridge between the ruby and the finger. All soldering is performed using traditional torch work followed by ultrasonic cleaning and final polishing, the white gold elements receiving rhodium plating post assembly to secure color consistency, and the entire piece undergoing multi stage quality control for symmetry, stone security, and finish uniformity.

The ruby and the precious metals are sourced with documented ethical provenance, reflecting a commitment to responsible supply chain practices. The gold used in both the yellow and white components is sourced from Fairmined and recycled sources on request, and each lot is traceable through chain of custody documentation, providing transparency from mine to finished piece. The ruby is sourced from mines and trading partners who adhere to environmental management protocols, including water stewardship, controlled tailings management, progressive rehabilitation, and minimization of landscape disruption, and the supply chain is subject to independent third party audits to verify compliance with labor standards and fair remuneration practices. Artisanal and small scale mining partners engaged in the procurement are enrolled in community development programs that fund local infrastructure and education, and the procurement process includes verifiable commitments to eliminate child labor and forced labor from operative phases. Where treatments are applied to enhance the gem, for example heat treatment to improve clarity and color stability, full disclosure is provided and an independent gemological report accompanies the ring on request, ensuring buyers receive complete technical information. This approach to responsible sourcing is combined with rigorous craftsmanship, providing a piece that not only exemplifies refined faceting and metalwork, but also meets contemporary expectations for ethical accountability and traceability.

Each coral cabochon carries the natural grain and sheen that only authentic sea born coral can provide, a color born of depth and centuries of reef growth. Complementing the corals are six black fancy shaped cabochon cut onyxs, weighing a total of 0.50 carats, with a clarity grade noted as not applicable and a color saturation described as dark. These deep dark onyx accents come from classic gemstone districts where cutters traditionally seek dense uniform black material that reads like liquid shadow next to the coral warmth. Set entirely in platinum 950, the composition elevates the organic warmth and the volcanic black into a striking contrast, while the secure handcrafted settings preserve the stones physical integrity and provenance story for generations.

Owning this ring means joining an exclusive circle of collectors who value origin as much as beauty, a bespoke experience curated by The Natural Gemstone Company. Because the corals and onyxes were sourced with attention to traceable origin and selectivity, only a very limited number of rings with this precise combination of color, cut and weight can be realized. The combination of ten vivid salmon corals and six dark onyx cabochons arranged around a central motif creates a design language that is simultaneously rare and unmistakably refined. For the discerning owner, the ring is not merely adornment, it is a testament to responsible sourcing, to craft that honors where each stone came from, and to a level of exclusivity that cannot be mass produced. If you seek a piece that signals membership in an elite group of collectors who appreciate provenance and scarcity, The Natural Gemstone Company welcomes your inquiry, and will ensure that this rare platinum creation is presented with the documentation and care that its origins and rarity deserve.

title: 4.09 Ct. Blue Paraiba Tourmaline Ring 18K White Gold J11469
availability: This item is available to ship now
descriptionHtml:
This 18K white gold ring presents a vibrant oval teal center stone that demands attention from the first glance, framed by a luminous halo of round brilliant diamonds that magnify its presence, the entire silhouette executed in rich 18K white gold for a premium finish and enduring lustre. Compared with mass market pieces that rely on single band solitaires or heavy bezels that mute a gems life, this design is deliberately architectural, allowing the centre stone to breathe and to shine. The halo functions as an optical enhancer, increasing perceived size and creating a ring of reflected light that makes the teal colour appear deeper and more electric than it would alone. Where low grade settings and thin plating can dull colour, the full 18K white gold construction here offers a stable, highly polished canvas that complements the blue green hue without overwhelming it, offering a warmer, more luxurious white than lower karat alloys while remaining more accessible than platinum in terms of value.

The way the ring is built guides the eye directly to the centre stone, through a combination of elevation, contrast and graduated sparkle, a raised prong installation lifts the oval slightly above the halo so that incoming light reaches the pavilion and returns as vivid colour and fire, the surrounding halo captures and amplifies those flashes, and the split shank pavé continues the sparkle down the shoulders so the gaze travels naturally from band to halo to centre. Compared to bezel settings that conceal the stone edge, the open prong halo here exposes the gemsc outline and depth, which is essential for showcasing the internal movement and natural character of a richly coloured centre. The pavé diamonds are closely matched and set to minimise metal sightlines, this creates uninterrupted rows of scintillation that act like a photographic frame, directing attention inward to the teal oval. The gallery is open and finished, permitting light from beneath which improves brilliance and allows the stone to display lively tonal shifts as the wearer moves, features that are rarely prioritized in lower cost rings that focus on quick manufacturing over optical performance.

From a value and longevity standpoint this ring outperforms many competitors in its class, 18K white gold provides a superior balance of purity and durability compared with lower karat white golds, the higher gold content gives a richer tone and more luxurious patina, and because the metal is professionally finished and rhodium plated, the white contrast with the diamonds and the teal centre is immediate and enduring. Against platinum alternatives you gain a lighter, equally white aesthetic at a favorable price point, without sacrificing a premium look, and against silver or gold plated fashion pieces you receive a true heirloom quality that will withstand daily wear with proper care. The design itself is timeless yet distinctive, the halo and split shank combination feels classic while offering a contemporary jewel like intensity not often found in run of the mill engagement offerings. For anyone considering a ring that must make a statement while still reflecting refined craftsmanship and lasting value, this 18K white gold halo ring positions the centre stone as the unquestioned focal point, it highlights colour, enlarges presence, and creates a level of optical drama that helps you stand apart from the ordinary.

descriptionHtml:
A sovereign expression of refined taste, this ring centers on a GIA certified, transparent purplish red rhodolite garnet of extraordinary presence, weighing 10.89 carats, fashioned into an elegant oval measuring 16.00 by 12.80 millimeters, and brought to life with a mixed brilliant cut that maximizes fire and depth. The gem’s vivid color intensity and excellent polish are immediately apparent, a vivid tableau of raspberry and wine that shifts with every micro-movement of the hand, while its eye clean clarity affords an unencumbered window into the stone’s velvety heart. Unenhanced and of Tanzanian origin, this rhodolite is a rare combination of natural purity and spectacular hue, set within a couture halo of sixteen straight baguette cut natural diamonds totaling 1.30 carats, and twelve round brilliant natural diamonds totaling 0.36 carats, their F color and VS clarity grades selected to provide an immaculate bright white contrast without distraction. The entire composition is sculpted in platinum 900, a metal chosen as much for its enduring luster as for its structural strength, the perfect frame to showcase a center stone that commands attention and admiration, and a testament to the exacting standards of The Natural Gemstone Company.

When one considers the practicality of such a remarkable jewel for everyday life, durability is paramount, and this rhodolite garnet performs admirably. On the Mohs scale rhodolite garnet typically registers around 7 to 7.5, placing it below sapphire and ruby at nine, and well under diamond at ten, but still within the range that permits regular wear when the stone is thoughtfully set and cared for. Hardness resists surface abrasion and scratching, while toughness measures a gem’s resistance to breakage; rhodolite garnets have good toughness for garnet family stones, and this specimen’s eye clean clarity and excellent polish indicate strong structural integrity. Compared to a sapphire or ruby, a rhodolite will require slightly more circumspection against hard blows or rough, repeated abrasion, yet it is far more resilient than many softer colored gems, and superior to delicate stones that cannot stand daily use. The ring’s design anticipates real life, the platinum 900 gallery and secure prongwork rising to protect the garnet’s girdle and pavilion, while the surrounding baguette and round diamonds act as an elegant buffer, absorbing incidental impact and focusing the eye on the central bloom of color. For those who wear their jewels as daily signatures, this ring offers a balance of captivating presence and practical resilience, provided simple precautions are observed, such as removing the piece during heavy manual tasks, avoiding prolonged exposure to harsh chemicals, and having the setting inspected periodically.

Owning this ring is to possess an heirloom-quality study in color, balance, and craft, a piece that speaks to accomplishment and discerning taste. The design’s elevated profile allows light to enter and animate that vivid purplish red heart at every angle, a spectacle intensified by the meticulous baguette and brilliant diamond arrangement that rims the garnet like city lights around a jewel of evening. Because the stone is natural, untreated, and GIA certified, the provenance and authenticity deliver confidence alongside beauty, assurances that align with the exacting service ethos of The Natural Gemstone Company. For longevity, simple at-home maintenance with a soft cloth, warm soapy water and gentle brushing will preserve brilliance, while professional cleaning and a routine prong check will ensure the setting holds its precision for years to come. The result is a ring that is not merely an accessory, but a visible measure of refinement, a confident emblem that endures, day by day, moment by moment, for those who choose to wear their finest intentions on the hand.

title: 2.52 Ct. Greenish Blue Paraiba Tourmaline Earring Platinum 950 J11585
availability: This item is available to ship now
descriptionHtml:
These drop earrings are executed entirely in platinum nine hundred fifty, a dense and durable alloy chosen for its neutral white tone and its ability to secure fine faceting without compromising light performance. The design centers on a pronounced pear shaped focal gem, cut in a modified brilliant pear to balance length with face up surface area, mounted in a low profile prong collar that exposes the pavilion to maximize light return. Surrounding the central pear is a halo of smaller pear and round brilliant accents, each matched for hue and cut profile to create uniform refraction across the surface. The settings employ precision hand setting with tightly controlled prong geometry and a ventilated gallery, the result being an open architecture that increases brilliance and facilitates cleaning, while millimeter level finishing on bezel rims and gallery edges ensures consistent reflections across the metal surface.

The visual impact arises from the deliberate size contrast between the central stones and their peripheral companions, the central pear being substantially larger in table and depth than each surrounding accent, creating a focal anchor that the eye is naturally drawn toward. The surrounding stones are graduated in size and alternate shape to form a radiating pattern, this radial scaling amplifies perceived size through repetition, and the close proximity of high clarity accents produces intense scintillation that makes the central stone appear even more substantial. In hand and worn images the drop reads as a refined yet present scale, the central pear commanding attention while the halo sustains that presence with continual micro sparkles, this interplay between a dominant face up area and numerous smaller facets heightens movement and light play as the wearer turns their head.

From a color and craftsmanship perspective the stones present a saturated bluish green tone with even saturation across all components, faceting precision has been controlled to maintain consistent windowing and to avoid dark zones in the center. Cut symmetry among accents preserves optical continuity, and the use of platinum nine hundred fifty not only secures the stones mechanically but also complements the cool color temperature of the gems, reinforcing the perceived clarity. The posts and backs are engineered for stability with discreet reinforcement at the drop junction to prevent lateral twist, a small but critical detail that keeps the face of the earring presented for maximum visibility, collectively these attributes explain why the stones catch and hold the eye, through size contrast, cut harmony, and meticulous setting technique.

descriptionHtml:
For centuries opal has been treasured as a stone of mystery and heritage, and the pair of oval Black Opal, Dark Opal, earrings offered by The Natural Gemstone Company continues that long tradition with a design that feels both ancient and perpetually modern. These opaque Australian Black Opal, Dark Opal, cabochon cut gems present a vivid play of color across deep, nocturnal fields, evoking the glamour of classical jewelry once guarded as family treasures. With a total weight of 0.74 total carat weight, eye clean clarity at face up inspection, and an excellent polish, each stone measures 6.13 x 4.53 x 2.12 mm, dimensions chosen to honor the balanced proportions found in historic signet and devotional pieces. Enhancement doublets are noted, and the skilled selection of doublet opals allows the bold, multi color flashes to be showcased while respecting the material traditions of opal mounting that generations of jewelers have refined. The stones speak of provenance and legacy, their Australian origin linking them to the storied fields where dark opals were first elevated to mythic status.

The craftsmanship behind the precise gemstone placement is rooted in centuries of technique, translated into exacting modern practice to protect and enhance the opal beauty. Each stone is entirely set in 14K yellow gold, the warm metal chosen to frame and intensify the vivid colors without overpowering them, and the bezel mounting is hand formed and hand finished to cradle the cabochon profiles with perfect alignment. Setting a doublet opal demands careful control of pressure and the subtlest allowances for thickness, and our setters place each gem so that the tabletop and girdle sit true, maintaining even metal walls at the same time the leverback suspension is balanced for elegant movement. Soldering and polishing stages are executed with minimal heat exposure near the opal, and final polishing is done by hand to achieve the excellent surface sheen that complements the vivid color intensity. The result is an heirloom ready pair that marries the romance of ancient gemstones with meticulous techniques, an offering from The Natural Gemstone Company that invites ownership, celebration, and careful stewardship for generations to come.

Accenting the spinels are a thoughtful configuration of natural white diamonds, specifically two kite shaped brilliant cuts totaling 0.16 carats, and fifty eight round brilliant cuts totaling 0.39 carats. The kite diamonds, positioned to flank the emerald cut spinels, function as transitional stones, their elongated shapes echoing the geometry of the central emerald cuts and guiding the eye along the line of the earring. The round brilliants serve as close set accents that break up the visual plane with lively scintillation. The provenance and untouched nature of the spinels, along with the assessed clarity and color of the diamonds, combine to define the technical quality of these earrings as much as their aesthetic impact. title: 3.50 Ct. Pink Spinel Earring 18K White Gold J12755
availability: This item is available to ship now
descriptionHtml:
A quiet poem of metal and color rests against the ear, a pair of earrings cast entirely in 18K white gold, each one a small stage where light and hue perform. At the heart of each piece, a cushion of pink gleams, like the first blush of dawn folded into a gemstone. Around that center, a carefully choreographed halo of baguette and brilliant cut diamonds encircles the pink, each facet a tiny mirror that amplifies the stone’s warmth, and a delicate scalloped gallery lifts the composition, giving it breath and movement. The white gold is cool and luminous, a silvered canvas that makes the pink appear to float, the milky sheen of the metal tempering the color into something both vibrant and refined. When you lift these studs to your ear, you feel attention to detail in the precise prongs, the evenness of the halo, the reassuring weight of 18K gold, a whisper of luxury that sits confidently but never loudly.

The pink at the center is what turns a simple stud into a memory kept near the skin, a saturation that arrests the eye without shouting, a tone that reads as romantic rather than theatrical. In sunlight the stone breathes, depths of cranberry and rose catching and releasing light, in indoor light it becomes softer, a petal pink with a core of lively fire. The surrounding diamonds, set in white gold, act as translators for that color, breaking it into scintillating notes that suggest movement and life. The coolness of the metal gives the pink a crystalline clarity, so that every nuance of saturation is legible, from the blush at the edges to the richer heart. There is a balance here, a deliberate choice to let the pink hold center stage while the diamonds and 18K white gold underline its romance, the overall effect being at once intimate and extroverted, a secret told brightly.

To understand the pink’s saturation, it helps to imagine it beside several beloved earring archetypes. Compared with classic white diamond studs, which speak in pure, icy brilliance with almost no hue, these pink centers command a chromatic presence that feels intimate and human, they invite stories rather than reflect only light. Against morganite studs, known for their soft, pastel whisper of peachy-pink, these earrings read as more vivid, deeper in the core, a shade that carries more life and persistence. Place them near traditional pink sapphire studs and you will find kinship and distinction, pink sapphires can range from delicate to deeply saturated, and these stones sit in a sweet middle ground, more lively than a pale morganite, and perhaps more floral and romantic than some intensely heated sapphires that verge into neon territory. Compared to rubies, which pulse with unabashed red intensity, these pinks are gentler, carrying warmth without the urgency of true red, a mood that says forever and also now. Against blue sapphire or emerald studs, which command with cool depth or verdant intensity, the pink creates contrast, it is the warm note in a palette of jewel tones, softer than the blue’s midnight, and more lyrical than the green’s forest. Champagne or cognac diamonds bring a whisper of warm brown, they are subtle and earthy, whereas these pink centers stay distinctly colored, refusing to merge into neutral. Finally, when set in rose gold, pink stones can sometimes vanish into warm metal, here in 18K white gold the pink is elevated, given space and contrast, its saturation becomes a statement rather than a match.

These earrings are for the person who wants color with composure, saturation that announces itself but also sings softly, a romance that fits both candlelit promises and the casual poetry of everyday life. Pair them with a simple white blouse and they become a punctuation mark of feminine confidence, wear them with an evening gown and they read as heirloom, intimate and incandescent. The 18K white gold setting will preserve the cool backdrop against which the pink lives, its alloy chosen for longevity and shine, the diamonds around the center ensuring that every tilt of the head scatters light like folded starlight. For care, gentle cleaning with a soft brush and mild soap will keep the white gold bright and the diamonds lively, periodic professional checks of the prongs will preserve the integrity of the setting, so that the saturation of the pink remains uninterrupted by wear. Imagine, then, these studs as both a gift and a ritual, each time you clasp the backs you are choosing a color that speaks of blushes and late afternoon light, a saturation that is memorable without claiming all attention, an everlasting whisper worn close to the heart.

title: 6.74 Ct. Blue Aquamarine Necklace 14K Yellow Gold J12568
availability: This item is available to ship now
descriptionHtml:
This necklace is a considered study in proportion, color and gemstone quality, set entirely in 14K yellow gold. The principal composition comprises twelve blue pear shaped mixed brilliant cut aquamarines, together weighing 6.74 carats, each graded very very slightly included with intense color saturation. Complementing these are eleven white round natural diamonds, together weighing 0.70 carats, with a clarity grade of SI2 and an H color designation. The stones are individually linked along a fine gold chain to form an articulated line that follows the natural curve of the collarbone, finished with a secure clasp. The mixed brilliant treatment applied to the pear shapes increases internal scintillation while preserving the elegant teardrop silhouette, producing a steady play of light as the piece moves. The round diamonds are deployed as measured accents, their combined weight calibrated to provide bright, intermittent flashes that punctuate the aquamarine sequence without overwhelming it. The warm tone of 14K yellow gold provides a restrained contrast to the cool, aqua blue of the aquamarines, and the overall execution emphasizes clarity of form and refined restraint, consistent with quality standards upheld by The Natural Gemstone Company.

The necklace takes clear cues from classic station and garland styles that have been part of fine jewelry language for more than a century, where evenly spaced gems create a rhythmic border around the neckline. In that historic vocabulary the garland or station approach reads as composed and symmetrical, intended to draw the eye along a continuous line. This design updates that tradition through contemporary choices in scale and finish, introducing a modern twist through lighter spacing, cleaner metal lines and the use of mixed brilliant cutting on pear shapes to amplify sparkle within a smaller silhouette. Instead of heavy bezel work or ornate metal filigree commonly associated with older pieces, this necklace uses minimal gold links and discreet settings to let the gemstones dictate the visual experience. The result is a piece that retains the formal restraint and balance of a classic station necklace, while speaking to today s preference for jewelry that layers with other pieces and reads equally well with casual and formal attire. The measured alternation of pear and round stones creates a subtle kinetic rhythm, a contemporary reinterpretation of a time honored composition.

From a technical and practical perspective the combination of very very slightly included aquamarines and SI2 diamonds is chosen with appearance and value in mind. The aquamarines offer exceptional color saturation which tends to be the most perceptible contributor to overall visual impact, and their high apparent clarity allows the mixed brilliant facets to function efficiently as light collectors. The diamonds, graded SI2, provide economical brilliance and sparkle, their H color placing them in a near colorless category that complements the aquamarine without introducing warmth or tint. The choice of 14K yellow gold balances everyday durability with a classic hue that complements skin tones and enhances the blue stones. Care instructions are straightforward and consistent with fine colored gemstone jewelry, including gentle cleaning with warm water and mild detergent, avoidance of harsh chemicals and professional inspection of settings on a periodic basis to confirm security of the links and clasp. Detailed grading and weight information accompanies the piece, and further documentation or specific measurements are available on request. For questions regarding certification, customization or additional imagery, please contact The Natural Gemstone Company, where these specifications are recorded and where experienced staff can provide further technical information.

descriptionHtml:
This necklace, crafted and entirely set in 14K yellow gold, brings together a considered pairing of gemstones that balances cool serenity with warm romance. The design includes four blue pear shaped mixed brilliant cut aquamarines weighing a total of 0.90 carats, and four pink pear shaped mixed brilliant cut sapphires weighing a total of 0.95 carats. Each aquamarine is graded as very slightly included, with a medium color saturation that reveals a clear sea like blue when viewed in natural light. Each pink sapphire is likewise graded as very slightly included, with an intense color saturation that produces a vivid pink hue prized by collectors and connoisseurs. The mixed brilliant pear cuts were chosen to enhance both scintillation and color face up, ensuring that each stone exhibits lively flashes of light while maintaining a pleasing, elongated silhouette that complements the graceful curve of the neckline.

From a gemological perspective, the clarity grade of very slightly included indicates inclusions that are minor, typically visible only under magnification to a trained eye, and rarely distracting to the naked observer. This clarity is an excellent balance for colored gemstones, allowing the natural color to take precedence while still offering durability and value. Color saturation is a primary driver of value in colored stones, and the medium saturation of the aquamarines provides a fresh, wearable blue that pairs beautifully with the intense, strongly saturated pink of the sapphires. The mixed brilliant cut combines facets oriented to maximize brilliance with a pavlovian play of light, while the pear shape provides a classic, feminine outline that elongates the neck. The decision to set these stones in 14K yellow gold adds a warm architectural frame, the gold surface reflecting warm undertones into the gem colors and enhancing the visual contrast between the cool aquamarine tones and the warm pink sapphires. For buyers who appreciate provenance, aquamarines are commonly sourced from classic deposits such as Brazil and Madagascar, while pink sapphires are often found in Sri Lanka, Madagascar, and other gem producing regions, though specific origins may vary from one parcel to another.

Beyond the technical attributes, this necklace is designed to carry personal significance and to become part of the wearer story. A necklace like this can commemorate a milestone, embody a memory of travel to a favorite seaside place, or celebrate an intimate relationship through the pairing of blue and pink stones that signify calm and affection. Because each gemstone is individually set and visible along the strand, the piece functions as a chain of moments, each pear shaped gem representing an occasion or sentiment that can be worn close to the heart. The combination of colors creates a lively but refined palette that adapts to both everyday wear and more formal moments, empowering the wearer to build an emotional connection with their jewelry over time. At The Natural Gemstone Company we take pride in sourcing and presenting gemstones that are both beautiful and meaningful, offering clients the opportunity to choose pieces that reflect their values and their memories. For an educated buyer who values clarity, color, and craftsmanship, this necklace offers an intersection of technical quality and emotional resonance, and The Natural Gemstone Company stands ready to provide additional certification details or to discuss customization that will make the piece uniquely personal.

The result is a piece whose exterior gloss belies the slow, deliberate care that produced it.

Wearing this necklace is an act of continuity, a way to bring tradition into daily life with subtlety and grace. It is a necklace intended to travel through seasons and generations, adaptable enough for ritual evenings and quiet afternoons, yet substantial enough to become an inherited mark of taste. At The Natural Gemstone Company, we consider this work a continuation of a lineage of craftsmanship, where responsibly sourced materials, expert cutting, and attentive setting coalesce into an object meant to be loved, worn, and passed on.

availability: This item is available to ship now
descriptionHtml:
This delicate bracelet from The Natural Gemstone Company is composed of seven oval shaped cabochon cut white opal stones set in 14K yellow gold, with an overall length of 7 inches. The seven multi color white opals weigh a combined 3.01 carats, and are characterized by intense color play, which is the primary determinant of value for opal. As cabochon cuts, the stones have been shaped to maximize the play of color and to present uniform, convex surfaces that enhance the apparent depth of color. In opal grading terms these pieces would be evaluated primarily on body tone, transparency, and play of color. The body tone for these stones is light, consistent with white opal, and the gems exhibit strong, lively flashes across multiple hues. Clarity for opal is assessed differently than for faceted gems, focused on the presence or absence of fractures, potch areas, and inclusions that interrupt color. These cabochons show clean polished surfaces with no visible fractures at normal viewing distances, and the translucency is typical for light opals, providing a soft glowing appearance which is highly sought after by collectors and connoisseurs.

Beyond the gem technicals, this bracelet represents a responsible choice for buyers who prioritize ethical sourcing and transparency. The Natural Gemstone Company sources materials through vetted suppliers who adhere to traceability practices and fair labor standards, and we work to ensure that our gold and gemstones are procured in ways that minimize environmental impact and support local communities. When origin documentation is available we provide it, however the specific origin for these white opals is unknown, which is clearly stated so buyers can make informed decisions. For care, opal benefits from gentle handling, avoidance of harsh chemicals and prolonged water immersion, and protection from sudden temperature changes, and routine inspection of the bezels and clasp will maintain long term wearability. For buyers seeking additional assurance we can provide condition notes and independent appraisal services on request, making this 14K yellow gold white opal bracelet both an elegant adornment and a transparently sourced piece for the knowledgeable purchaser.

title: 6.02 Ct. Multi Color Opal Bracelet 14K Yellow Gold J10909
descriptionHtml:
This bracelet draws its inspiration from the meeting of light and water, a theme long celebrated in both nature and jewelry history. The arrangement of four multi color oval cabochons evokes a river of opalescent pools, each stone reflecting green, blue, and warm amber flashes like sunlight passing through rippling water. The 14K yellow gold setting references the warmth of sunlit banks, while the surrounding halo of brilliant cut diamonds reads like glints of sunlight on a moving surface. The design nods to historical tastes for luminous gemstones found in Victorian and Art Nouveau pieces, but with a modern clarity of presentation that allows each Crystal Opal to remain the star. This piece is presented by The Natural Gemstone Company, crafted to appeal to collectors and connoisseurs who value provenance, technical grading, and thoughtful design.

From a technical standpoint the bracelet is a serious offering for an educated buyer. The piece measures a total of 10 inches in length, and centers four oval double cabochon cut Crystal Opals from Ethiopia, weighing a combined 6.02 carats. These opals are graded eye clean with vivid color saturation, characteristics that speak to strong play of color and transparency common to high quality crystal opal specimens. The double cabochon cut enhances depth and internal fire, allowing color layers to read clearly under varied light angles. Accenting these stones are 62 natural round brilliant cut white diamonds, totaling 0.70 carats, graded VS1 for clarity and F for color. The VS1 clarity means inclusions are extremely slight under 10x magnification and do not interfere with visual performance, while the F color sits in the near colorless range for strong contrast against the vivid opals and warm gold. The entire composition is set in 14K yellow gold with secure prong and bezel work to protect cabochons. For care, note that Ethiopian crystal opals can be sensitive to rapid temperature change and harsh chemicals, so gentle cleaning with mild soap and a soft cloth is recommended, avoiding ultrasonic cleaners. For collectors seeking a wearable, museum quality example of natural opal beauty, this bracelet combines verified gem grading, desirable origin, and refined setting to deliver enduring value.

title: 9.42 Ct. Blue Aquamarine Bracelet 14K Yellow Gold J11155
availability: This item is available to ship now
descriptionHtml:
This bracelet is a study in timeless elegance, a classic line of luminous pale blue gemstones, each entirely set in 14K yellow gold, that traces the wrist with a refined and steady rhythm. The stones are carefully faceted to maximize the play of light, creating a soft, watery glow that shifts with every movement, and the warm tone of the yellow gold embraces each gem, amplifying its clarity and radiance. The design reads as both personal and ceremonial, suitable for days of quiet routine and evenings of ceremonial grace, and its proportions have been imagined to sit comfortably against the skin while remaining visually present. Worn alone it is understated and eloquent, paired with other pieces it becomes part of a symphony, and whether seen at a distance or admired at close range, the bracelet carries a quiet confidence that never demands attention, it simply receives it.

Blue gemstones have held a special place in human history, associated with the depths of the sea and the breadth of the sky, symbols of tranquility, protection, and steadfastness. Since antiquity, noble houses and sea farers alike believed that stones of this hue offered calm and clarity, and jewelers through the ages have set them in gold to create objects meant to endure across generations. The combination of cool blue and warm gold is a motif that recurs in classical jewelry from many cultures, a visual language that speaks of balance, endurance, and good fortune. The craftsmanship of this bracelet echoes those long traditions, where each setting is considered, and where the metal and the stone are married in a way that honors both materials. Owning such an object is to participate in a lineage of appreciation for finely made treasures, the same appreciation that inspired ancient artisans to craft pieces that were meant to be more than adornment, they were to be companions through the seasons of life.

When you choose this bracelet as a gift, you offer more than an object, you offer a story that can grow with the wearer, a tangible expression of regard that can be worn daily or reserved for moments that mark new beginnings. The steady procession of matching stones around the wrist can signify a series of shared memories, each gem representing a chapter, and the gold that binds them speaks of permanence and value. For anniversaries, birthdays, milestone achievements, or as a token of reassurance in times of change, this bracelet translates sentiment into something that will deepen in meaning with age. It is the kind of present that can be presented alone in a quiet exchange, or placed beside other tokens as part of a larger ritual, and when handed over it conveys intention, forethought, and a wish for continuity. The very materials, gemstones set in 14K yellow gold, suggest longevity, and the bracelet can become an heirloom, carried forward to mark new unions, new births, and the passage of years.

Beyond its emotional resonance, this bracelet is practical for everyday life and for the ceremonial moments that punctuate it, it layers effortlessly with both contemporary and traditional wardrobes, from linen dresses and crisp shirts to tailored evening wear. To preserve its beauty, simple care will suffice, occasional gentle cleaning with warm water and a soft cloth will restore its natural luster, and safe storage when not worn will keep the gold bright and the stones clear. The bracelet invites personalization through the way it is worn and paired, and for a loved one it will serve as a constant reminder of connection, a physical presence that accompanies them through daily routines and special occasions alike. Selecting this bracelet is to choose a piece that honors the past, enriches the present, and promises to be a cherished part of the future.

title: 15.93 Ct. Blue Tanzanite Brooch 18K White Gold J11446
availability: This item is available to ship now
descriptionHtml:
The centerpiece is a pear shaped, highly saturated blue gemstone, cut in a mixed faceting scheme that combines a modified brilliant crown with an elongated pavilion to maximize depth of color and controlled light return. The crown facets are proportioned to create strong contrast and scintillation across the table, while the pavilion angles are calibrated to prevent windowing and to concentrate the rich blue tone. The length to width ratio is deliberately maintained in the elegant range for a teardrop silhouette, producing a graceful drop that reads larger on the finger and on fabric. Facet junctions are crisply executed, producing sharp facet reflections and a pleasing pattern under magnification, indicative of meticulous lapidary control. The stone presents as eye clean in normal viewing, with even color saturation that remains vivid under incandescent and daylight balanced illumination, suggesting careful material selection and expert cutting to preserve optical performance.

Surrounding the center gem is a precision set halo of round brilliant white stones, individually faceted to a consistent cut grade to deliver uniform brilliance and fire. The diamonds are bead set in shared prongs that are micro finished to minimize metal visibility and to produce a continuous halo that amplifies perceived center size and color contrast. The entire composition is fabricated in 18K white gold, with a hand pierced gallery and multi prong basket that opens the pavilion to optimize light return and to reduce weight without compromising strength. The reverse shows tidy solder joints and dovetailed prong shoulders, the work of skilled bench hands who combined machine precision with hand finishing. The white gold is finished with a high polish and rhodium surfaced plating to enhance white body color and to protect against wear. Practical considerations include a secure clasp and reinforced bail, routine care recommendations for periodic cleaning and professional inspection, and the option for bespoke adjustments to fit a particular mounting or chain, all executed with the same technical attention to proportion, symmetry, and optical balance that define this piece.
